children.text: rājñoktam saṃprati pañcabhūtātmakasya tasya gatibhedena nāmabhedamāha jalaga iti ||
children.translated_text: What was stated by the king has been given; now he explains the difference of names for that substance, composed of the five elements, according to difference of motion: 'water-going.'

children.text: yaḥ pārado jalarūpeṇa jalasvabhāvena gacchati sa jalago jalagativiśiṣṭa ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: The mercury which moves in the form of water, with the nature of water, is called <s>jalaga</s>, that is, characterized by water-like motion.
Gold and the other metals that consist of it are of that nature.
Even substances such as <s>rasa</s>, whose essence is stable, are of that nature.
Their density and stability arise only through conjunction with earth, impurity, and slag.

children.text: ata eva drutirūpeṇaiva teṣāṃ sthitiḥ sambhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore their existence is possible only in a molten form.
The nature of water is a form of downward movement.
Even in metals that are pure and molten, downward movement is indeed observed.

children.text: yaḥ pāradastvaritastvarayā vegena yukto nātyucchritam ākāśe gacchati kiṃtu bhūmisaṃnihitākāśe bhuvi ca sa haṃsaga ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: The mercury which is swift, endowed with quickness and speed, does not go very high into the sky, but moves in the sky close to the ground and on the earth; that is called <s>haṃsaga</s>.
Because it goes through the sky like a <s>haṃsa</s>, it is <s>haṃsaga</s>.
It is found in substances such as mayūra and gaṇḍūpada.

children.text: yastu malarūpeṇa kṛṣṇavarṇenāṃśena viśiṣṭo gacchati sa malaga ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: But that which moves marked by a black-colored portion in the form of impurity is called <s>malaga</s>.

children.text: yaśca sadhūmo dhūmena dhūmasamānavarṇordhvarekhāsahitākāśagatyā saha vartata iti sadhūmaḥ sa dhūmaga ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: And that which is smoky, accompanied by smoke, that is, by an upward line in the sky of the same color as smoke, is called <s>dhūmaga</s>.
It is found in haritāla, hiṅgula, manaḥśilā, rasaka, gaurīpāṣāṇa, and the like.
For it is experienced that these burst because of obstruction of smoke and then rise upward.

children.text: nābhiyantrabhūdharalohamūṣādiyantrādinā nirdhūmajāraṇāyāmapi mahatā prayatnenāpi teṣāṃ sthiratvaṃ mīmāṃsyaṃ bhavati bhavennanveti ||
children.translated_text: Even when smokeless digestion is performed by devices such as a navel-apparatus, bhūdhara apparatus, iron crucible, and so on, and even with great effort, their stability has to be examined: will it occur or not?
There is another, fourth motion of mercury.
That is called the living motion.
The living motion is a motion invisible like that of a living soul.
Therefore it is also called divine.

children.text: tasyā devagaterivādṛśyatvāttayā yuktaḥ sa pārado'ṇḍājjīva ivādṛśyagatyā yuktaḥ svasthānānniṣkramennirgacchati ||
children.translated_text: Because that motion, like the motion of a deity, is invisible, mercury endowed with it comes out from its own place, as a living being comes from an egg, endowed with invisible motion.

children.text: aṇḍāddehasya nirgamanaṃ dṛśyate dehasahitasya jīvasya tu bahirnirgamanaṃ na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: The emergence of the body from the egg is seen, but the outward emergence of the living soul together with the body is not seen.

children.text: bālasya cālanaśvāsocchvāsādikriyayā cānumīyate tadvad asyāpīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is inferred from the child's actions such as movement, inhalation, and exhalation; the meaning is that the same applies to this mercury too.

children.text: tayā gatyā yukta evāyaṃ jīvānprāṇino jīvayettena sa raso jīvanāmnā smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Only when endowed with that motion does it enliven living beings; therefore that <s>rasa</s> is remembered by the name 'living.'

children.text: kārayettaṃ saṃskāranipuṇavaidyahastena rājā tatsamo vasumānvātmanaḥ prajānāṃ ca rakṣaṇārtham iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that a king, or a wealthy man equal to him, should have that operation performed by the hand of a physician skilled in the procedures, for the protection of himself and his subjects.

children.text: tadevābhrakaṃ bhūmimadhye rājahastāt sapādahastād adhastād adhobhāgasthaṃ yat khanijaṃ ghanam abhrakaṃ vajrākhyaṃ tad eva pūrvoktaguṇam ||
children.translated_text: That same mica: the dense mica, called vajra, which is mineral, located in the middle of the earth, below the king's hand by one and a quarter hastas, and situated beneath, possesses the qualities previously stated.
But the other kind should be known as without essence, because of contact with wind, water, urine, impurity, heat, and worms.
This is an indicative statement applying to all mineral substances.
For in general, only when they are situated in the womb of the earth do they possess their complete inherent qualities.
Here, although the word 'dense' denotes mica in general, it culminates in vajra-mica.
For that alone has the qualities just described.

children.text: grāsābhāve hyupoṣita iva rasaḥ kāryakaro na bhavedityāha sacandrikamiti ||
children.translated_text: For in the absence of food, <s>rasa</s>, like one who has fasted, would not be effective; therefore he says 'with moonlight.'
<s>Sacandrika</s> means possessing glittering brightness.
<s>Kiṭṭābha</s> means containing abundant slag.

children.text: grasitaśca grasitābhrasattva eva lohe svarṇādyutpādane lohamāraṇe rogavāraṇārthaṃ lohaprayoge ca niyojyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when it has swallowed it, that is, when it is indeed mercury that has swallowed the essence of mica, it is to be applied in metal for producing gold and the like, for killing metals, and in the use of metal for warding off disease.

children.text: tathā rasāyane jvarāṅkuśādi tattadrase rasāyane ca lakṣmīvilāsavajrapañjarādirūpe vakṣyamāṇa ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise it is to be used in <s>rasāyana</s>, in particular preparations such as jvarāṅkuśa, and in rasāyanas to be described, such as Lakṣmīvilāsa and Vajrapañjara.

children.text: rasa īyate prāpyate'neneti vyutpattyātra rasaśabdena rasarasāyanayoḥ saṃgrahāt ||
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>rasa</s>, by the derivation 'that by which rasa is obtained,' includes both <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: tatastadabhrakaṃ dhānyābhrakaṃ kṛtvā matsyākṣikārasenaikadinaparyantaṃ saṃmardya cakrīṃ vartulasthūlavaṭikāṃ vidhāyāvaśoṣya śarāvasaṃpuṭitaṃ kṛtvārdhe'bhrake puṭe puṭed ardhe'bhrake puṭam ardhagajapuṭaṃ tacca gajapuṭagatārdhabhāgaṃ vanopalaiḥ pūrayitvā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then that mica, after being made into dhānyābhraka, should be triturated for one day with the juice of matsyākṣikā, made into a round thick pill called a cakrī, dried, enclosed in a pair of earthen saucers, and roasted in a half-mica pit; a half-mica pit is a half-gajapuṭa, and that is made by filling half the space of a gajapuṭa with forest cow-dung cakes.
'It should be roasted' means it should be cooked.

children.text: pratipuṭam abhrakasya mardanaṃ tataścakrīṃ kṛtvā viśoṣya śarāvasaṃpuṭitaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: At each roasting there should be trituration of the mica; then, after making it into a cakrī and drying it, it should be enclosed in earthen saucers.

children.text: koṣṭhyām avaśiṣṭasattvaṃ kācakiṭṭasaṃśliṣṭaṃ kaṇarūpaṃ durgrāhyaṃ tattu agnau śānte sati samāhṛtyaikīkṛtya bahir niṣkāsya saṃkuṭya vicūrṇya tatsaṃśliṣṭaṃ kaṇasattvaṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: The remaining essence in the furnace, joined with glassy slag, is in granular form and hard to grasp; when the fire has gone out, one should collect it, combine it, take it outside, pound it, pulverize it, and remove the granular essence joined with it.
One should separate it from the slag and take it.
Some say that <s>vimala</s> is silver-mākṣika.
But that is not correct.

children.text: tāramākṣīkasya guṇair alpāntaro 'pyayaṃ tatparyāyo bhavituṃ nārhati ||
children.translated_text: Although this differs only slightly from tāramākṣika in qualities, it cannot be its synonym.
Because there is no authority for that in lexicons and similar sources.
And because otherwise the separate statements of the definition, differences, purification, essence, and qualities of vimala, as distinct from tāramākṣika, would become pointless.

children.text: athoddeśakramānurodhena tutthavarṇanāntaraṃ capalaṃ varṇayati gaura iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, in conformity with the order of enumeration, after the description of tuttha he describes capala with the words 'white,' and so forth.

children.text: ayaṃ padārtho vyāvahārikanāmnāsmin deśe loke na prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This substance is not well known among people in this region by its practical name.
It is inferred that this is a particular kind of stone found in the earth's interior near a zinc mine.

children.text: āṅglabhāṣāyāṃ reḍiyam iti nāmnopalabdhaḥ padārtho 'yam eveti kecit ||
children.translated_text: Some say that this very substance is what is known in the English language by the name radium.
The artificial one, however, will be described in the chapter on technical terminology.
Now he describes <s>rasaka</s>, which has come next in the order of enumeration, with the words 'rasaka' and so on.
<s>Rasaka</s> is a mineral earth which is the source material of <s>jasada</s> (zinc).
Its essence is produced as exactly equivalent to <s>jasada</s>.

children.text: khaṭhikā khaḍu cās iti nāmnā loke prasiddhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khaṭikā</s> is well known in common speech by the names khaḍu and cās.
He states its two varieties with the words 'sphaṭikī' and 'pītikā'.

children.text: sphaṭikīlepācchatavāraṃ tāmrapatraṃ lohapatraṃ prati vā liptā satī tatpaścāt caret pāradena prayojyakartrā cārayed bhakṣitāṃ kārayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When a copper sheet or iron sheet has been smeared a hundred times with a coating of <s>sphaṭikī</s>, then one should cause it to move with mercury used as the agent; that is, one should cause it to be consumed.
For it is used in digestion as a <s>viḍa</s>-substance.
Here the verbal root <s>car</s> contains an implied causative sense.
<s>Sauvīra</s> is black-colored surmā, in the vernacular.
That is <s>rasāñjana</s>.

children.text: etad rasod iti brijabhāṣāyām uttaradeśe prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: In the northern country this is well known in Braj speech as rasod.

children.text: etad rītikiṭṭajanyaṃ dāruharidrākaṣāyājadugdhapākajanyaṃ tu rasāñjanam ityapi vadanti ||
children.translated_text: They also say that this is produced from brass dross, while what is produced by cooking a decoction of <s>dāruharidrā</s> with goat's milk is also called <s>rasāñjana</s>.
Next, <s>srotoñjana</s>.
It is well known in the world as white-colored surmā.
Next, <s>puṣpāñjana</s>.
This is produced from brass flower.
It is well known in the Maharashtrian language as jastaphūl.
Next, <s>nīlāñjana</s>.
It is well known in the world as blue-colored surmā.
He states another opinion with the words 'some'.

children.text: katicidvadanti kiṃ tejivāhānāṃ prabalavegasāmarthyaviśiṣṭāśvānāṃ nālaṃ sadyojātānāṃ teṣāṃ nābhinālaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhamiti ||
children.translated_text: Some say: what is the navel-cord of the <s>tejivāhana</s>s, horses endowed with powerful speed and force, namely the umbilical cord of those just born, is <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>.
Now he describes <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, which has come next in order, with the word 'himavat' and so on.
And it is yellow in color.
It is a mineral small stone, also of animal origin, marked by smooth, numerous, sparkling plates.
Both are of two kinds: <s>nalikā</s> and <s>reṇuka</s> are the mineral varieties.

children.text: kampillaḥ kṣudrapāṣāṇaviśeṣaḥ kapileti nāmnā loke prasiddho gaurīpāṣāṇo dāruṇaviṣarūpo'yaṃ pāṣāṇaviśeṣaḥ somala iti mahārāṣṭrabhāṣāyāṃ prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kampilla</s> is a particular small stone, known in the world by the name kapilā; this <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> is a particular stone in the form of a terrible poison, known in the Maharashtrian language as somala.
<s>Agnijāra</s> is the distinctive fetal membrane of a crocodile cast out from the ocean.
<s>Girisindūra</s> is a particular red-colored substance found inside mountain rock.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is powdered mercury, well known in the world by its own name.
<s>Moddāraśṛṅga</s> is well known in common speech as murdāśiṃga.

children.text: trividhasya tasya svarūpamāha yaḥ kiṃcit pītavarṇo vikaṭakarāla āhataḥ saṃcūrṇarūpo bhavati sa gaurīpāṣāṇa ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: He states the form of its threefold variety: that which is somewhat yellow, misshapen and dreadful, and when struck becomes powdered, is called <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s>.
This same one is marked by a brilliance like crystal.
This qualifier may also apply to the second variety.
The second is conch-like, and it too is marked by brilliance.

children.text: tṛtīyabhedāpanno yaḥ sa tu haridrābho haridrāsamānaḥ pūrṇapītavarṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one belonging to the third variety, however, is like turmeric, similar to turmeric, and entirely yellow in color.
Among the three, each preceding one is superior to the one following it.
Now he explains <s>girisindūra</s> with the words 'in great mountains' and so on.
<s>Alpīyaḥ</s> means extremely small.
This is generally not obtained in the world.

children.text: kecittu kāmiyāṃ sindūra iti nāmnā prasiddho'yaṃ padārtho'tiraktavarṇa iti vadanti ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, say that this substance is well known by the name kāmiyāṃ sindūra and is extremely red in color.
But the one very well known in the world is indeed that produced from lead.

children.text: sa eva cātra grāhya iti rāvaṇamatam ||
children.translated_text: And that alone is to be accepted here; this is <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s opinion.
Because of his statement, 'sindūra is lead-born.'
Now he describes <s>hiṅgula</s>, which has come next in the order of enumeration, with the word 'hiṅgula'.
This <s>rasa</s> is a particular mineral earth of mercury.
For this very reason it was said in the first chapter:

children.text: tāṃ mṛdaṃ pātanāyantre pātayanti rasaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: 'They distill that earth in a distillation apparatus; from it comes <s>rasa</s>,'
so the verse says.
An artificial one is also seen in the world, produced by cooking mercury, sulfur, and navasāgara.
This mineral one is of two kinds.
He states the characteristic of the best of these with the word 'śvetareṣa' and so on.

children.text: sa ca haṃsapāka iti nāmnā kathitaḥ pākena vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it is called by the name <s>haṃsapāka</s>, being prepared by cooking.
Because it is marked by white and red color.
This is the best.
The first, however, having inferior white streaks, has few virtues.
It is called <s>carmāra</s>.
In the Gurjara region, that is, in the Gurjara country,

children.text: arbudagireḥ pārśve nāgakhanisthānabhūte ca jātam utpannaṃ yad viśiṣṭaṃ kṣudrapāṣāṇātmakaṃ dravyaṃ sadalapītavarṇātmakaṃ tanmṛddāraśṛṅganāmnā prathitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the distinctive substance of the nature of a small stone, born beside Mount <s>Arbuda</s>, in a place that is a lead mine, and having a petal-like yellow color, becomes famous by the name <s>mṛddāraśṛṅga</s>.
He states its properties with the words 'lead essence' and so on.
It is the source material, the cause, of lead essence.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> is rāuṭī in Braj speech.
<s>Garuḍodgāraka</s> and <s>tārkṣya</s> are two other synonyms for <s>marakata</s>.
It is well known in the world as pannā.
<s>Puṣparāga</s> is well known in the world as pukhrāj.
<s>Mahānīla</s> is <s>indranīla</s>.
<s>Padmarāga</s> is ruby.

children.text: vaiḍūryaṃ tad yadākāśe sajalameghaśabdād aṅkuraviśiṣṭaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> is that which, when there is the sound of a rain-cloud in the sky, develops a sprout-like mark.
For this very reason it has another synonym, <s>abhraloha</s>.
This is well known in the world as pirojā.
<s>Kaṇḍarānvita</s> means furnished with hollows; <s>sirāvṛta</s> means covered with veins.
Now he states the general defects common to all gems, with the words 'grāsa' and 'trāsa'.
<s>Grāsa</s> is the condition of having one part swallowed or eaten away.
A trāsa is the condition of being marked by dirt both outside and inside.
Bindu is well known.
And it is of many kinds.
Rekhā is well known.
Jalagarbhatā is water-inclusion.

children.text: yatrāntaḥ koṭara ivāntaḥ śuṣiraviśiṣṭajalābhāso bhavati tādṛśatvam ||
children.translated_text: It is the condition in which inside, as if in a hollow, there is the appearance of water distinguished by an inner cavity.
Now he describes vaidūrya, with the words 'vaidūryam' and so on.
In the common language this is known as laśanyākhaḍā.
It is even and broad.
With the word 'moving about'.
It has within it an appearance like a trembling white cloth.
That is threefold and furnished with sixteen colors.

children.text: te ca varṇā granthāntare viśiṣṭadravyasāmyam udāhṛtya pṛthakpradarśitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those colors are separately shown in another treatise by citing likenesses to particular substances.
White is like a white hibiscus flower; balakṣa is in the flower of the plantain;
arjuna is said by the learned to be in the water-lily.
A pale color occurs in dust, and also in the flower of the ketakī;
hariṇa should be precisely indicated in a yellow, variegated, and white substance.

children.text: dhūsaro bakule puṣpe kṛṣṇaḥ syād atasīsume
children.translated_text: Dhūsara is in the bakula flower; black occurs in the flower of the atasī;
hari is in the leaf of the śirīṣa; red is remembered in the red lotus.
When red is mixed with black it is aruṇa; when white is mixed with red it is
pāṭala. And in a monkey it is kapiśa, in black-red.
It may be smoky; piṅga has the appearance of rocanā; and then there is piśaṅgaka.
Karburā is remembered in lotus-dust and as like a rainbow.
So it is said.
He states the well-known gold produced from mines with the words 'there and there'.
Of mountains.

children.text: ete ca girayo himālayavindhyasahyakarṇāṭakasthanīlagiriprabhṛtayaḥ svarṇakhanisthānatvena prasiddhāḥ santi ||
children.translated_text: And these mountains, such as the Himalaya, Vindhya, Sahya, Karṇāṭaka, and Nīlagiri, are known as places of gold mines.

children.text: kāṣṭhāṃ prāptau pītaraktavarṇau paripūrṇau vihāya caturdaśavarṇapūrṇaṃ khanijaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When full development has been reached, apart from the fully developed yellow and red colors, the mineral contains fourteen colors.

children.text: ratnaparīkṣakaisteṣāmeva varṇānām utkarṣavibhājakā yāvacchataṃ vikalpitāḥ kakṣā loke prasiddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among gem-examiners, up to a hundred classes that distinguish degrees of excellence among those very colors are known in the world.
There are two mines of copper.
Of these, what is found in one mine is known as nepāla.
Nepālī is kunaṭī.
Because it has the same red color as that.
Or it is named nepāla because the mine is near the country of Nepāla.
Alternatively, this is an established conventional name.
But what is found in another mine is called mleccha.

children.text: yathā mlecchadhātur aspaṣṭaśabde tathā spaṣṭaśabdaraktavarṇatvānmleccham iti saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: Just as the mleccha metal is so called in reference to indistinct sound, so this is named mleccha because its red color is clear-sounding, that is, clear in character.

children.text: yat paruṣaṃ kaṭhoraṃ pogaronmuktaṃ pogaram alakavat kuṭilarekhās tābhir muktaṃ tadrahitam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is rough, hard, and free from pogara means free of pogara, that is, free from curved lines like curls.
The word pogara occurs here.
And its meaning is not excluded.

children.text: ato bodhārthaṃ tatparyāyān āha aṅgachāyā ca vaṅgaṃ cikuraṃ ca iti pogarasyābhidhātrayaṃ nāmatrayam asti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for understanding, he states its synonyms: aṅgachāyā, vaṅga, and cikura are the three designations, the three names, of pogara.
Thus these names mean a particular form of luster.
Because the lines have a white sheen like tin, it is called vaṅga.
Because the gleams have the form of hair, the shape of hair, it is also named cikura.

children.text: yad uktam eva kharalohaṃ tadyadi lohādbhaṅguraṃ lohamayaghanaghātena bhaṅguraṃ bhavati paraṃtu pogaraṃ pogaraviśiṣṭaṃ dṛśyeta tarhi tat kharaloham api paramuttamaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: If the same khara-loha that has been mentioned, though brittle from iron and made brittle by the blow of an iron hammer, is nevertheless seen to have pogara, to be marked by pogara, then even that khara-loha is regarded as supremely excellent.

children.text: tasya cokto vyastaḥ samasto vā bhedo'yaṃ jāraṇāyāṃ sakaladhātubhakṣaṇārthaṃ pāradasya mukharūpo bhavatītyāha ekadvitrīti ||
children.translated_text: And he says that this distinction of it, whether separate or combined, becomes the mouth-form of mercury in jāraṇā, for the purpose of consuming all metals, with the words 'one, two, three'.

children.text: kevalabhrāmakasattvasya prathamaṃ yathāvidhijāraṇenāpi pāradasya mukhaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Even by the prescribed jāraṇā of the essence of bhrāmaka alone first, a mouth is produced for mercury.
Then the mercury consumes all metals and the like.
Therefore even a certain single variety becomes a mouth of mercury.
That which has that one is one-mouthed.

children.text: bhrāmakacumbakayoḥ sattvadvayasyaikīkṛtasya yathāvidhijāraṇena pāradamukhaṃ kṛtaṃ cet saṃyuktabhedadvayaviśiṣṭaṃ tat kāntaṃ dvimukham ucyate ||
children.translated_text: If, by the prescribed jāraṇā, a mercury-mouth has been made from the two essences of bhrāmaka and cumbaka combined into one, then that kānta, distinguished by two joined varieties, is called two-mouthed.
The meaning should be understood in just this way for three-mouthed and the rest.

children.text: vijātīyadravyagrāsāntarasahitam apyetat prathamaṃ jāritaṃ cenmukhaṃ bhavatītyataḥ sarvatomukham ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: Since this also, if first digested together with the swallowing of heterogeneous substances, becomes a mouth, it is called all-faced.
The meaning is that this mouth is distinguished by homogeneous and heterogeneous varieties, separate and combined.
With 'it is not beneficial'.
There, because it is impure through admixture with nāga.

children.text: tiryagākārā tiraścīnā yā dīrghā cullī āhāﾱa iti mahārāṣṭrabhāsāyāṃ prasiddhā tasyāṃ ghaṭaṃ tiryagvaktram etādṛśaṃ ghaṭaṃ nyased adhiśrayet ||
children.translated_text: In a long transverse furnace, called by a Maharashtrian vernacular name, one should place, that is set upon the fire, a pot with its mouth turned sideways.

children.text: taṃ ghaṭaṃ ca vaktraṃ vinā bāhye samaṃ tato'ṅgulasthūlaṃ mṛdā gopayellepayet ||
children.translated_text: Apart from the mouth, one should cover that pot evenly on the outside, that is smear it with clay to the thickness of one aṅgula.
Into that apparatus called the bhṛṣṭa-yantra one should put lead measuring twenty palas.

children.text: tasmin drute sati ekakarṣaṃ śuddhasūtaṃ tatra kṣiptvā tato darvyā vighaṭṭya itastataḥ saṃcālyaikībhūte satyarjunādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ kṣāraṃ palamitaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: When it has melted, one should put into it one karṣa of purified mercury; then, after stirring it with a ladle and moving it here and there, when it has become unified, one should add a pala of alkali from each of arjuna and the other plants.

children.text: tato dorbhyāṃ lohadarvyā vighaṭṭayaṃścālayan viṃśatirātraparyantaṃ tīvrāgninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: Then, stirring and agitating it with an iron ladle held in both hands, one should cook it with a fierce fire for twenty nights.

children.text: tena vidhinā nāgabhasma raktavarṇaṃ kapotacchāyaṃ kṛṣṇamiśraraktavarṇaṃ vā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: By that procedure, nāga-bhasma becomes red in color, dove-hued, or red mixed with black.
When <s>nāga</s> (lead), reduced to ash and free from defects such as causing heat and eruptions, becomes a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative preparation).
That brass is of two kinds.
The division is into <s>rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>.
Among these, <s>rītikā</s> has two varieties.
One is slightly coppery in appearance, and the other is golden-colored.
Vessels made of gold and the like are round bowls.
Kaṭatra means pieces of leather treated with astringent substances.
This is a long, four-cornered sieve.

children.text: tatra dīrghāḥ śalākāstiraścīnāśca vaṃśamayyaś catuṣkoṇakāṣṭhapaṭṭikāchidreṣu bahirnirgatāgrāḥ sūtrabaddhāḥ kāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In it, long rods and crosswise rods made of bamboo, with their tips projecting outward through the holes of four-cornered wooden strips, should be made fastened with thread.

children.text: kuṇḍalīṃ kuṇḍalākārāṃ vartulāṃ tṛtīyāṃ cālanīṃ vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should make a third sieve called <s>kuṇḍalī</s>, circular and having the shape of a ring.
<s>Vājivāla</s> means hairs from a horse's tail.
<s>Ambara</s> means cloth.
A bottom covered with either of those is called a bound bottom.
<s>Śarkarā</s> means very small fragments of stone.
White grains coarser than those are sugar-crystals.
Or by the word <s>śarkarā</s>, sand too should be understood.
Hard pieces of burnt wood alone have the names <s>śikhitra</s> and <s>kokila</s>.

children.text: saṃprati teṣāṃ sāmānyam avāntarabhedaṃ cāha śikhitrā iti ||
children.translated_text: Now he states their general character and subordinate distinction with the words 'śikhitrāḥ' and so on.

children.text: pāvakena vahninā bhuktvā ucchiṣṭāḥ parityaktā aṅgārāḥ śikhitrāḥ kokilāśca matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Coals that have been consumed by fire, that is, left behind and abandoned by fire, are regarded as <s>śikhitra</s> and <s>kokila</s>.

children.text: viśeṣastvittham vahninā bhuktvā svayaṃ tyaktāḥ śikhitrā haṭhāt pratikūlavāyudhūlikṣepamṛttikādinipīḍanādinā yatnena vahnito viyojitā aṅgārāḥ kokilā matā iti ceti ||
children.translated_text: But the distinction is as follows: coals consumed by fire and left by it of their own accord are <s>śikhitra</s>; coals forcibly separated from the fire by effort, such as by adverse wind, by throwing dust, or by pressing with earth, are regarded as <s>kokila</s>.

children.text: te prajvalitā jalena vinā nirvāṇāḥ kṛtā vahnimuktāḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When blazing, they have been extinguished without water, that is, made free from fire.
<s>Śaṅkhikā</s> means small vessels made of conch-shell.
<s>Kṣuraka</s> means particular razors belonging to a barber.
<s>Pākya</s> means alkali of barley.
<s>Pālikā</s> means a ladle.
<s>Karṇikā</s> is called <s>vilī</s> in the language of Maharashtra.
Here it should be understood as having a circular row of tooth-like points.
Now he states the definition of <s>kajjalī</s> with the words 'with metals'.
And the metals are:

children.text: svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ ca tāmraṃ ca raṅgaṃ jasadameva ca
children.translated_text: gold, silver, copper, tin, and indeed zinc,

children.text: sīsaṃ lohaṃ ca saptaite dhātavo girisaṃbhavāḥ
children.translated_text: lead and iron: these seven are the metals born from mountains.
So it is said.
By the word 'first' there is inclusion of orpiment, realgar, and the like.
And by the word 'and' there is inclusion of secondary metals.

children.text: teṣāṃ bhāgo rasasamo viṣamo vā yathopadeśaṃ grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of these, a portion equal to mercury, or unequal, should be taken according to the instruction.

children.text: saiva kajjalī dravaṃ dattvā marditā cedrasapaṅkasaṃjñāṃ labhate ||
children.translated_text: That same <s>kajjalī</s>, if triturated after adding a liquid, receives the name <s>rasapaṅka</s>.
The use of <s>kajjalī</s> should be understood as being for the preparation of <s>rasasindūra</s> and the like.
He will state the use of <s>rasapaṅka</s> for the preparation of <s>Trailokyasundara-rasa</s> and the like.
Now he states the definition of <s>piṣṭī</s> with the words 'arkāṃśa' and so on.
It means from an amount equal to half a <s>niṣka</s>, that is, measured as a half-<s>niṣka</s> portion.
From sulfur equal to an <s>arka</s>-part: in relation to mercury, the word <s>arka</s> denotes the number twelve.

children.text: tatsaṃkhyākā ye'ṃśā bhāgā niṣkārdhātmakā bhāgāstattulyād rasāt pāradāt ||
children.translated_text: Those parts, whose number is twelve, are portions each consisting of half a <s>niṣka</s>; from mercury equal to those, namely from <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
The expression 'half a <s>niṣka</s>' is an indicative term for any quantity that has been taken.

children.text: tena gandhakasya yo bhāgastato dvādaśaguṇitaḥ pāradabhāgo'tra grāhya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the meaning is that here a portion of mercury twelve times the portion of sulfur should be taken.

children.text: yathoktabhāgam ubhayaṃ pṛthaggṛhītvā tīvre'rkātape lohe khalve truṭiśa īṣanmānena punaḥ punardattvā mardanānnavanītarūpā mṛdulā navanītākhyā ca piṣṭī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Taking both in the stated proportions separately, and then in strong sunlight in an iron mortar adding them bit by bit, in slight quantities, again and again, by trituration there comes to be a soft <s>piṣṭī</s>, butter-like in form and called <s>navanīta</s>.

children.text: atra navanītākhyo gandhako bhakṣyaḥ pāradaśca bhakṣakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the sulfur called <s>navanīta</s> is what is eaten, and mercury is the eater.
But it remains the same in the various forms of <s>piṣṭī</s>.
Therefore this is called <s>navanīta</s> by the name of what is eaten, which indicates the distinction.
Its other name is <s>gandhakapiṣṭī</s>, sulfur-paste.
Now he states the definition of <s>pātanapiṣṭī</s> with the words 'one-fourth part' and so on.

children.text: caturthāṃśaṃ śuddhaṃ svarṇacūrṇaṃ pāradamadhye prakṣipya taptalohakhalve 'mlarasena jambīrādijena yāmaparyantaṃ dviyāmaparyantaṃ vā mardanena saṃjātā cūrṇarūpā sā hemapiṣṭikāpi pātanopayogena siddhikaratvāt pātanapiṣṭir ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Putting one-fourth part of purified gold powder into mercury, and triturating it in a heated iron mortar with an acidic juice produced from citron and the like for one yāma or for two yāmas, the powder-form substance that arises is also <s>hemapiṣṭikā</s>; because it brings success through its use in pātana, it is called <s>pātanapiṣṭī</s>.

children.text: tādṛśīṃ piṣṭiṃ kṛtvā pātanāyantre 'dhasthapātrāntastala ūrdhvabhājane vā liptvā praharacatuṣṭayaparyantam agniyogenordhvaṃ pāradaṃ pātayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made such a <s>piṣṭī</s>, one should smear it for pātana in the lower vessel of a pātana apparatus, on its inner surface, or in the upper vessel, and by the application of fire for four praharas one should distill the mercury upward.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ pāradāt pṛthagbhūtvādhobhāgasthatatsvarṇacūrṇam ūrdhvalagnapāradaṃ ca yantrād bahirniṣkāsyaikīkṛtya punastaptalohakhalve'mlena rasena pūrvavanmardayitvā pūrvavat pātayet ||
children.translated_text: After that, when the gold powder has separated from the mercury and is situated in the lower part, and the mercury adhering above has been removed from the apparatus, one should unite them, again triturate them as before in a heated iron mortar with acidic juice, and distill them as before.

children.text: evaṃ śatadhā pātanena kṣīṇo gatirahito nirdoṣaḥ pāradaḥ sthiro'gnisaho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by a hundredfold pātana, the mercury, diminished, motionless, and free from defects, becomes stable and able to withstand fire.

And then, through the sequence of jāraṇā beginning with seed substances and the like, with very little effort it also grants the highest accomplishment, namely the capacity to transform body and metal.
Now he states the definition of <s>kṛṣṭī</s> with the word 'silver'.
<s>Jātarūpya</s> means gold.
By the word 'and so on', pyrites, cinnabar, and the like are included.

children.text: tairmāritaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pañcamitrasaṃskāreṇa prakṛtyavasthāpannaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Made dead by those substances, and again and again restored to its natural state through the procedure with the five friends.

children.text: evaṃ saptavāraṃ daśavāraṃ votthāpitasvarṇatāraṃ ca krameṇa hemakṛṣṭī tārakṛṣṭī cābhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Gold and silver that have been raised up in this way seven times or ten times are respectively called <s>hemakṛṣṭī</s> and <s>tārakṛṣṭī</s>.

children.text: rasagandhādiyogena malavyapohanād ujjvalam utkṛṣṭaṃ sārūpyaṃ svarṇaṃ tāraṃ cetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the combination of mercury, sulfur, and the like, because the impurities are removed, it becomes bright and excellent; this means gold and silver having the same appearance.
One should cast that gold-<s>kṛṣṭi</s> into melted gold of deficient color.

children.text: tena kṣepeṇa varṇo na hīyate tatsvarṇaṃ hīnavarṇaṃ na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: By that casting-in, the color is not diminished; that gold is not seen as deficient in color.
The meaning is that it appears full in color.

children.text: evameva hīnavarṇatāre tārakṛṣṭyāḥ kṣepeṇāpi tāraṃ pūrṇavarṇaṃ bhavatītyartho'pi bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In exactly the same way, it should also be understood that, when silver-<s>kṛṣṭi</s> is cast into silver deficient in color, the silver too becomes full in color.
Made means prepared, that is, processed.

children.text: bījaṃ śuddhaṃ svarṇotpādakaṃ lohadhātvādipāradasya pītavarṇatvakaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The seed, being pure and productive of gold, should make mercury from iron, minerals, and the like yellow in color.
In the eighth chapter of the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, the venerable authorities also stated the <s>kṛṣṭi</s> of mercury.

children.text: atha hemaraktītāraraktyor lakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ cāha tāmramiti ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the definition and result of gold-redness and silver-redness with the word 'copper'.

children.text: tīkṣṇalohena samabhāgena saṃyuktam ekīkṛtaṃ tāmraṃ bahuvāraṃ drutaṃ kṛtvā gandhakasahite lakucarase nirvāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Copper, joined and made one with an equal portion of sharp iron, should be melted many times and quenched in lakuca juice mixed with sulfur.

children.text: tadvallohamiti khyātaṃ tārasya rañjanī drute tasminnikṣepeṇetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is known as tadvalloham; it colors silver when, while it is melted, it is cast into it. This is the meaning.

children.text: tāraraktīkaraṇārthaṃ tu varalohena tāram eva dhamanenaikīkṛtya raktīkṛtaṃ kāryaṃ sāpi rūpyasya bījānāṃ ca rañjanī raktavarṇotpādikā ||
children.translated_text: But for making silver red, silver itself should be united with superior iron by blowing and made red; that too colors silver and seeds, producing a red color.

children.text: saṃprati tāradalasya svarṇadalasya ca lakṣaṇamāha mṛteneti ||
children.translated_text: Now he gives the definition of silver-foil and gold-foil with the word 'with dead'.

children.text: mṛtena bhasmībhūtena pāradena yena kenaciddravyeṇa baddho yaḥ pāradastena baddhapāradena mṛtena lohena vā sādhitaṃ saṃskṛtam anyalohaṃ vijātīyaṃ lohaṃ sitatvam upāgataṃ prāptaṃ śvetavarṇaviśiṣṭam athavā pītatvam upāgataṃ prāptaṃ pītavarṇaviśiṣṭaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: An alien metal processed with dead mercury, that is, mercury reduced to ash, or with mercury bound by some substance, or with bound mercury, or with dead iron, becomes white in character, having reached whiteness, or becomes yellow in character, having reached yellowness.

children.text: tatkrameṇa candradalam analadalaṃ svarṇadalaṃ śāstre prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: In that order these are known in the treatise as moon-foil, fire-foil, and gold-foil.
Fire means gold.
The meaning is artificial silver and artificial gold.
They are well known in ordinary usage by the name <s>ravā</s>.
Now he states the definition of <s>śulbanāga</s> with the word 'with pyrite'.

children.text: samabhāgamākṣikeṇa māritaṃ tāmraṃ pañcamitrasaṃskāreṇa samutthitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Copper killed with an equal portion of pyrite should be made to rise up through the processing with the five mitras.

children.text: evaṃ daśavāraṃ kṛtvā tadvattāmravanmākṣikeṇaiva māritaṃ viśuddhaṃ nāgaṃ tadubhayaṃ mithaḥ samaṃ catuṣpalamitaṃ gṛhītvā punar nīlāñjanena samabhāgena māritaṃ pañcamitrasaṃskāreṇa punarutthāpitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having done this ten times, one should likewise take pure lead, killed with pyrite just like the copper, take both of them together in equal measure, amounting to four palas, and again kill them with an equal portion of blue antimony and make them rise again through the processing with the five mitras.

children.text: evaṃ saptavāraṃ māraṇapūrvakotthāpanena saṃśuddham etaddravyadvaṃdvaṃ rasaśāstre śulbanāgamiti kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after being purified by seven repetitions of rising preceded by killing, this pair of substances is called <s>śulbanāga</s> in <s>rasaśāstra</s>.
He states its use with the word 'processed'.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ pāradena samabhāgena śuddhena sahājamūtreṇa saṃmardya vajramūṣāyāṃ dhmānena jātaṃ khoṭaṃ śodhanagaṇena saha dhmānācchuddhaṃ kṛtvā taṃ khoṭabaddhaṃ pāradaṃ mukhamadhye yo dhārayettasya mehasamūhanāśo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: If someone triturates that powder with an equal portion of purified mercury together with goat's urine, heats in a diamond crucible, purifies the resulting lump by heating it with the group of purifying substances, and holds that mercury bound into a lump in the mouth, for him the group of urinary disorders will be destroyed.
He gives the definition of <s>piñjarī</s> with the word 'metal'.

children.text: yathā jasadaṃ mūṣāyāṃ tāmre nikṣipya dhmānenaikībhūtaṃ patrajādyauṣadhīrase pītavargajarase vā nikṣepātpittalaṃ bhavati tadvadanyadapi tādṛgvarṇaṃ saṃkīrṇalohaṃ piñjarīvācyaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Just as zinc, placed into copper in a crucible and made one by heating, becomes brass by being cast into the juice of plants born from leaves or into juice produced from the yellow group, so any other mixed metal of such a color is called <s>piñjarī</s>.
That is what is denoted by the expression 'plant born from leaves'.

children.text: yasyā utpattau kāraṇaṃ bījasthāne patrameva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In its production, the cause in the place of the seed is precisely the leaf.
This plant, called cīritapattrā and having the form of a particular small shrub, grows in a garden.
He characterizes <s>candrārka</s> with the word 'parts'.
Āvartitā means made into the form of mercury that has been unified by heating.
Of bhāsvat, that is, of copper.
And the production of gold from <s>candrārka</s> by transmutation with mercury bound into a lump is taught in the <s>Rasasāra</s>.
Now he states the definition of <s>nirvāha</s> with the words 'in the metal to be treated'.

children.text: yasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ sādhyalohe nirvāhye lohe drute sati tasmiṃstatrānyalohaṃ vaṅkanālataḥ prakṣiptaṃ vaṅkanālajadhmānenaiva drutaṃ kṛtvā prakṣiptaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the operation in which the treatable metal, the metal to be subjected to <s>nirvāha</s>, has melted, another metal is cast into it through a bent tube; that is, it is melted and cast in by the blowing produced from the bent tube itself.
By saying 'bent tube', blowing produced by bellows and the like is excluded.
<s>Nirvāhaṇa</s> amounts to unification.
<s>Nirvāpaṇa</s> and <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> do not differ in meaning.
But the use of the word <s>nirvāpaṇa</s> in the sense of unification is not found at present.

children.text: kiṃtu sarvatra tadarthaṃ nirvāhaṇaśabda eva prayukto dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Rather, everywhere the word <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> alone is seen to be used for that meaning.
And this <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> is generally performed for the processing of seeds and the like.

children.text: yathā pāradodare bījānāṃ garbhadrāvaṇayogyatāsaṃpādanārthaṃ nirvāhaṇasaṃskāraṃ vyājahāra rasahṛdaye
children.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> he describes the <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> process for making seeds fit for melting in the womb, inside mercury:

children.text: mṛtanāgaṃ mṛtavaṅgaṃ mṛtavaraśulbaṃ mṛtaṃ tathā tīkṣṇam
children.translated_text: Dead lead, dead tin, dead excellent copper, and likewise dead sharp iron,

children.text: ekaikaṃ hemavare śatanirvyūḍhaṃ dravati garbhe ca ||
children.translated_text: each one, subjected to a hundred <s>nirvāha</s>s in excellent gold, melts in the womb.
Thus it is said.
The meaning is that, in gold of one part, any one among lead and the others should be subjected to <s>nirvāha</s> a hundredfold.
Gold processed in this way becomes an excellent seed.

children.text: atha nirvāpaṇadravyabhāgānuktisthāne taddravyasya kiyadbhāgaprakṣepaḥ kāryastadāha kṣipediti ||
children.translated_text: Now, where the portions of the substances for quenching have not been stated, he explains how many parts of that substance should be cast in, with the word 'one should cast'.
The meaning is that one should cast it in and carry it through.
Since casting in is common to both, when the measure of the substance to be cast in has not been stated, he also states it with the word 'to be cast in'.
The definition of <s>āvāpa</s> will be stated in this very chapter.
In the melted substance, beginning with metal, into which casting is to be done.

children.text: tatra bhāge dṛṣṭa ukte tu dṛṣṭavaduktabhāgamitameva tannirvāhaṇadravyam āvāpadravyaṃ ca kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: But when the portion has been seen or stated there, one should cast in only the substance for carrying through and the substance for <s>āvāpa</s> measured according to the stated portion, just as it has been seen.
He states the definitions of the various technical terms that indicate dead metal, with the word 'dead'.

children.text: tallohaṃ vāritaram ucyate yanmṛtaṃ sattoye prakṣiptaṃ taratīti ||
children.translated_text: That metal is called <s>vāritara</s> which, when dead, floats when placed in water.

children.text: tallohaṃ rekhāpūrṇamucyate yanmṛtam aṅguṣṭhatarjanīmadhye saṃmarditaṃ tayoḥ sūkṣmarekhāntaraṃ praviśediti ||
children.translated_text: That metal is called <s>rekhāpūrṇa</s> which, when dead and rubbed between the thumb and forefinger, enters into the spaces of the fine lines between them.
Now a fully dead metal is called <s>apunarbhava</s>.

children.text: yat pratyekaṃ samabhāgair guḍādibhiḥ samastaiḥ saha miśritaṃ piṇḍīkṛtaṃ mūṣāmadhye prakṣipya dhmānena prakṛtiṃ pūrvāvasthām āmalohabhāvaṃ na prāpnuyāditi ||
children.translated_text: That which, mixed with substances beginning with molasses, each in an equal portion, formed into a lump, placed inside a crucible, and blown with fire, does not return to its original nature, its former state, the condition of raw metal.

children.text: athottamākhyamṛtalohalakṣaṇamāha yadvā pūrṇamṛtaṃ yallohaṃ vāritaraṃ svapṛṣṭha upanītaṃ dhānyaṃ dhārayati ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the definition of the dead metal called excellent: or that fully dead metal which is <s>vāritara</s> and, when grain is placed on its surface, supports the grain.
The meaning is that it bears the weight of grain.

children.text: tatra lohe taddhānyaṃ kathaṃ tarati tadupamayāha yathā jale haṃsaviśeṣāstaranti tadvat tathā dhānyabhārasahaṃ tanmṛtaloham uttamam iti nāmnā śāstre kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: How does that grain float on that metal? He states it by a comparison: just as particular swans float on water, so that dead metal which bears the weight of grain is celebrated in the treatise by the name 'excellent'.

children.text: atra bahuṣu pustakeṣu ūnamaṃ parikīrtitam ityapi pāṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here in many manuscripts there is also the reading 'it is proclaimed as <s>ūnama</s>'.

children.text: tasya svayam ūnam ūnabhāraṃ laghvapi yallohaṃ svāpekṣayā gurudravyaṃ gurudhānyaṃ vā māti sahata iti vyutpattyā kliṣṭārthabodhakaḥ sa pāṭho nātipriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That reading is not very pleasing, since by the derivation that it measures or bears a deficient weight, or that even a light metal bears a heavy substance or heavy grain in relation to itself, it conveys a strained meaning.
Now he states the defining mark that gives this same dead metal called <s>apunarbhava</s> the designation <s>niruttha</s>, with the word 'with silver'.

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ melāpakamadhvājyaṃ dattvā mūṣāyāṃ saṃyojitaṃ na laget na sajjetaikībhāvaṃ na prāpnuyād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Joined means that, after giving honey and ghee as uniting substances and placing it in a crucible, it does not adhere, does not stick, and does not become one; this is the meaning.
And unification is to be understood from an increase in the measure of the silver.
And this has been clarified in the <s>Rasasaṃketakalikā</s>:
When the silver that has gone into iron, honey, and ghee becomes equal to its own measure,
then the iron is <s>niruttha</s>; otherwise one should process it again.
Thus.
Silver means pure silver.

children.text: atha jāraṇāsaṃskāre prakṣepārhasya bījasya lakṣaṇamāha nirvāhaṇeti ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the process of <s>jāraṇā</s>, he states the definition of the seed fit for casting in, with the word <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>.

children.text: nirvāhyate prakṣepeṇaikīkriyate 'neneti vyutpattyā nirvāhaṇaśabdena nirvāhakaṃ dravyaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: By the derivation 'it is carried through, that is, unified, by casting in by means of this', the word <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> should be understood as the carrying-through substance.

children.text: prakṣepeṇa guṇaviśeṣotpādanapūrvakaikībhāvasāmānyācca tena śabdena vāpanadravyasyāpi saṃgrahaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because there is the common feature of unification by casting in, preceded by the production of a special quality, the substance for <s>vāpana</s> should also be included by that word.
With precisely this intention, the reading 'by a particular <s>nirvāpaṇa</s>' is also seen.

children.text: tena nirvāhaṇena nirvyūḍhaṃ yadbījopādānarasalohādi tattadvarṇaṃ nirvāhaṇadravyasya samānavarṇaṃ śāstranirdiṣṭavarṇaṃ ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever source-seed, mercury, metal, and so on has been carried through by that <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>, it becomes of that color, the same color as the <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> substance and the color prescribed by the treatise.

children.text: vāpanadravyeṇa mṛdu ca bhavettathā sattvabhasmotpādakavidhibhyāṃ ca prāptamārdavam ||
children.translated_text: And through the <s>vāpana</s> substance it becomes soft, and likewise softness is obtained through the procedures that produce essence and ash.

children.text: tathā kṛto vicitrasaṃskāro garbhadrāvako raktavargakaṣāye niṣecanarūpo melāpakadravyasaṃyogādiśca yasyetyevaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ rasaśāstre siddhabījamityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: And what possesses such qualities as a manifold processing that makes it a womb-melter, quenching in decoctions of the red group, and conjunction with uniting substances and the like, is called a perfected seed in <s>rasaśāstra</s>.

children.text: bījaṃ dvividhaṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ ceti bhedāt ||
children.translated_text: Seed is twofold, by the distinction of yellow and white.
And each of those is also twofold.
Natural and artificial.

children.text: yaddhi khanisambhūtaṃ śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ rajataṃ vā tad akṛtrimam ||
children.translated_text: For pure gold or silver that has arisen from a mine is natural.

children.text: yattu dhāturasoparasasaṃyogakriyāviśeṣajanitasvarṇarajatotpādanayogyatāsaṃpannaṃ pītaṃ svarṇarītyādi śvetaṃ vaṅgādi tatkṛtrimam ityācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: But what is yellow, such as gold-colored brass and the like, or white, such as tin and the like, possessing the capacity for the production of gold or silver generated by a special operation of combining metals, mercury, and secondary minerals, they call artificial.
Each of those again is twofold.
Pure and mixed.
Pure means each single one; mixed means mutually blended.
Again, all this is threefold.
Conceived, colored, and cooked.

children.text: tatra tatkalpitaśabdavācyaṃ yacchuddharasoparasaśuddhamāritaṃ mithaḥ saṃyuktaṃ miśraṃ vā lohādidvaṃdvīkṛtam ekaikaṃ sattvakaraṇavidhinā nirvāhaṇena dvaṃdvamelāpakavidhinā ca militaṃ śuddhaṃ jātamārdavaṃ tad evaikībhāvaṃ vrajati ca raktādivargeṣu secanena prāptavarṇaṃ rañjitasaṃjñakaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Among these, what is denoted by the word <s>kalpita</s> is that which, whether pure or mixed, consists of purified mercury and secondary minerals, purified and killed, combined with one another or paired with metals and the like, either singly or in pairs, united by the procedure for producing essence, by <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>, and by the procedure for pairwise union, purified, having acquired softness, and then going into actual unification; and when it has acquired color through quenching in the red and other groups, it is called <s>rañjita</s>.

children.text: nirvāhaṇena hemaśeṣakṛtaṃ tāraśeṣakṛtaṃ vā yadbījaṃ bhūdharayantrādiṣu puṭitaṃ tatpakvabījaṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: The seed which, by <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>, has been made with gold remaining or with silver remaining and has been heated in devices such as the <s>bhūdhara-yantra</s>, they call cooked seed.
Thus this definition, as stated, should be understood as including all seeds.

children.text: atra rasoparasānāṃ śodhanaṃ tu sūryāvartādigaṇena kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, the purification of mercury and secondary minerals should be done with the group beginning with <s>sūryāvarta</s>.
Magnetite is purified by soaking with hare's blood.

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ patraṃ ca lavaṇakṣārāmlaravisnuhīkṣīrair liptaṃ dhmātaṃ paścānnirguṇḍīrase bahuvāraṃ niṣecitaṃ sacchudhyati ||
children.translated_text: Gold and silver foil, smeared with salt, alkali, sour substances, and the milks of <s>arka</s> and <s>snuhi</s>, blown with fire, and afterwards quenched many times in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, becomes properly purified.

children.text: nāgavaṅgaghoṣatāmrāṇi tu prataptāni nirguṇḍīrasasekais tanmūlarajaḥpravāpaiśca śudhyanti ||
children.translated_text: But lead, tin, bell-metal, and copper, when heated, are purified by sprinklings with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> and by castings of powder from its root.

children.text: sarvo'pi lohaḥ pratapto mākṣīkadaradavāpena bahuvāraṃ kṛtena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: Every metal, when heated, is purified by repeated castings of pyrite and cinnabar.
The <s>sattva</s>s of <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s should be extracted by the procedure stated in the root text.
Now I shall state the method for carrying out the seed, as taught in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>.
Next he states the technical term <s>tāḍana</s>, with the word "combined".

children.text: parisādhanaṃ dhmānenāvaśeṣakārakaṃ yadvaṅkanālena pradhmātaṃ prakarṣeṇa dhmānaṃ kriyate tadrasaśāstre tāḍanaśabdena kathitam ||
children.translated_text: The completion that causes a residue by blowing, namely what is strongly blown through a bent tube, is called <s>tāḍana</s> in <s>rasaśāstra</s>.

children.text: yathā ghoṣādvaṅgaṃ vināśya tāmrasyāvaśeṣārthaṃ dhmānaṃ tacca gārākoṣṭhyāṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: For example, there is blowing to destroy tin from bell-metal and leave copper as the residue; this should be done in a <s>gārā</s> furnace.
He states the definition of <s>sattva</s> with the words "alkali and acid".
Alkali means barley-alkali and the like.
Acid means citron juice and the like.
A solvent is molasses, bdellium, <s>guñjā</s>, and the like.
The group of solvents will be stated later.
The five products of the goat means substances such as the five products of the cow.

children.text: matsyādipiṇḍīdravyaṃ ca tadyuktaṃ tena piṇḍīkṛtaṃ rasoparasādi dravyam ||
children.translated_text: And the lump-making substance beginning with fish: a substance such as a <s>rasa</s> or <s>uparasa</s> joined with that, that is, made into a lump by it.
The mine-furnace: the mine will be described later.
The furnace is the text-section that is the place of description.

children.text: tatrokte yogye koṣṭhe koṣṭhayantre 'ṅgārakoṣṭhyādau ca mūṣāyāṃ prakṣipya yadā bhastrāvaṅkanālādinā dhmātaṃ syāttadā tato dravyād dravarūpo yaḥ sāro nirgacchati pṛthagākāreṇa nipatati tatsattvamucyate ||
children.translated_text: When, after placing the substance in the suitable furnace mentioned there, in a furnace apparatus such as a charcoal furnace, and in a crucible, it is blown with bellows, a bent tube, and the like, then from that substance the liquid essence that comes out and falls separately in a distinct form is called its <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: atha dhmānakriyāyā mānaviśeṣajñānārthaṃ kṛtāyāḥ kolīsakasaṃjñāyā lakṣaṇamāha koṣṭhikāśikhareti ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to know the particular measure of the blowing operation, he states the definition of the term <s>kolīsaka</s> that has been established, with the word "at the top of the furnace".

children.text: śikharaparyantaṃ paripūrṇakokilānāṃ dhmānena mūṣākaṇṭhaparyantaṃ yadāpacayo bhavati tāvaddhmānasyaikakolīsaka iti saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: When the loss, through blowing, of coals filled up to the very top reaches down to the neck of the crucible, that much blowing is termed one <s>kolīsaka</s>.
<s>Nāliśaka</s> is another synonym of this very term.
Now he explains mercury extracted from cinnabar, with the word "vidyādhara".
The <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus is of two kinds: without water and with water.

children.text: tatra prathamaṃ kanakasundaraprabhṛtirasānām ūrdhvabhāge puṭanārtham upayujyate ||
children.translated_text: Of these, the first is used for heating substances such as <s>kanakasundara</s> in the upper part.
And that is enclosed by a lower and an upper vessel.

children.text: yattu dvitīyam uttānapātraghaṭitaṃ tadatra vidyādharaśabdena grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: But the second, which is constructed with an upturned vessel, is what should be understood here by the word <s>vidyādhara</s>.
After the phrase "triturated with ginger," the word "from cinnabar" is to be supplied.
He states the definition of what is extracted from bell-metal, with the word "little".
<s>Tāḍita</s> means fully blown.

children.text: atra tālaḥ svalpaśabdena kāṃsyasya caturthāṃśena grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the word "little," the tin should be understood as one fourth of the bronze.
Its use should be understood as being for the destruction of tin after it has separated from the copper.
He states the definition of <s>varanāga</s> with the word "sharp".

children.text: samabhāganīlāñjanasaṃyutaṃ tīkṣṇalohaṃ samabhāgena ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvāndhamūṣāyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ sadyadā nāgāpekṣayāpyatimṛdu kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ śīghradrāvaṃ ca bhavettadaitad varanāgam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: When sharp iron combined with an equal portion of blue antimony is given an equal portion of borax and blown firmly in a closed crucible, and then becomes softer even than lead, black in color, and quick-melting, this is called <s>varanāga</s>.
One should stir it with water made from the ashes of <s>arka</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and plantain.
That clear water, filtered through cloth, should be taken in the sunlight.

children.text: mṛdukṛṣṭaṃ drutadrāvamiti pāṭhe dhmātvā mūṣātaḥ kṛṣṭaṃ bahirākṛṣṭaṃ śītaṃ sadapi saṃjātamārdavam agniyogena śīghradrāvaṃ ca bhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the reading "soft when drawn out and quick-melting," the meaning is that, after being blown and drawn out from the crucible, that is, pulled outside, it becomes soft even when cold and quick-melting when brought into contact with fire.
This is superior to lead; therefore it is <s>varanāga</s>.
This word is formed by placing the latter member first.

children.text: asyopayogaṃ tvasthirāṇāṃ kharparādisattvānāṃ sthirīkaraṇārthaṃ pūjyapādā udājahrū rasasāre ||
children.translated_text: As for its use, the venerable authorities have cited it in the <s>Rasasāra</s> for stabilizing unstable <s>sattva</s>s such as those of calamine.
Its procedure has indeed been explained here in the second chapter, in the commentary on the procedure for the <s>sattva</s> of <s>rasaka</s>.
But the reading "lead joined with blue antimony" is simply erroneous.
For it should be understood that lead is of no use in stabilizing <s>sattva</s>s.
He states the meaning of the word <s>utthāpana</s> with the phrase "of what is dead".

children.text: pāradarasoparasalohādīnām atimūrchitānāṃ prākṛtaguṇakriyāsahitānāṃ vā punarudbhūtiḥ punaḥ pūrvavat sthānāpannatvam utthāpanam ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: The re-emergence of mercury, <s>rasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, metals, and the like that have been very much stupefied, or that possess their natural qualities and actions, namely their restoration to a state like the former one, is called <s>utthāpana</s>.
He defines the technical term <s>ḍhālana</s> with the phrase "of a melted substance".

children.text: yathā varalohakavidhau satīkṣṇatāmrasya dhmānena drutasya lakucadrāve nikṣepo'trādhyāye prāguktaḥ sa ḍhālanaśabdena paribhāṣyate ||
children.translated_text: For example, in the procedure for superior iron, the casting of sharp copper, melted by blowing, into lakuca juice was previously stated in this chapter; here that is designated by the word <s>ḍhālana</s>.
Now <s>capala</s> is of two kinds.
It is a particular stone, and also an artificial substance in the form of a metal.
Of these, the particular stone was mentioned in the second chapter.
He states the definition of <s>dhauta</s> with the word "earth-serpent".
Earth-serpents are earth-worms.
Their dung is precisely a particular kind of earth, and it is found near them.
Its use for producing hard <s>sattva</s> has already been stated in the fifth chapter.
He states the definition of <s>bhajanī</s> with the phrase "greater than the portion of silver".

children.text: anuvarṇasuvarṇake hīnavarṇasuvarṇe hemakṛṣṭiṃ dattvā śatāṃśavidhinā raktapītavarṇotkarṣārthaṃ yatamānena sādhakena pramādātkāraṇāntareṇa vā yadā rūpyasya yo bhāgaḥ śāstra uktastaṃ vihāya pramāṇāpekṣayādhikaḥ kṣipyate tādṛśakṣepaṃ kṛtvā yadā varṇikāhrāse prāgavasthitapītavarṇasyāpi hrāsaḥ kṣayo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When, in gold of inferior color and in gold of deficient color, a practitioner who is trying to enhance the red and yellow color by the one-hundredth-part procedure after applying <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s>, through negligence or for some other reason, omits the portion of silver prescribed in the śāstra and adds more than the proper measure, then after making such an addition, when the coloring matter decreases, there is also a decrease, that is, a loss, of the yellow color that had previously been present.

children.text: athavā dravyair vedhādāvanupadiṣṭadravyair vaṅganīlāñjanādibhiḥ saṃmīlanenāpi yo varṇikāhrāsaḥ sā rasaśāstre bhañjanīti kathyate ||
children.translated_text: Or, the loss of coloring matter that occurs also through mixture with substances not prescribed for piercing and the like, such as tin, blue antimony, and so on, is called <s>bhañjanī</s> in <s>rasaśāstra</s>.
Now the definition of <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s> is as follows.
Silver or gold, struck by mercury, sulphur, and the like,

children.text: samutthitaṃ ca bahuśaḥ sā kṛṣṭī hematārayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and raised up many times: that is the <s>kṛṣṭi</s> of gold and silver.
This has already been stated before.
In the present procedure, <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s> is this:
Mercury, cinnabar, pyrite, sulphur, realgar, lapis lazuli, and mica,
copper killed by roasting, worked into silver: this is <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s>.
Thus it says.

children.text: rasadaradādīnāṃ puṭena mṛtaṃ yacchulbaṃ tattāre nirvāhitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the copper killed by the roasting of mercury, cinnabar, and the other substances should be made to penetrate into silver.
And the one-hundredth-part procedure is:
There should be ninety-eight parts of silver, one part of gold,
and one part of mercury: this is known as the one-hundredth-part procedure.
Thus in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>.

children.text: tatra nirvyūḍhatārabhāgasyādhikakṣepeṇānu varṇasuvarṇe varṇanāśaḥ spaṣṭa eva ||
children.translated_text: There, when an excessive addition is made to the part of silver that has been worked in, the destruction of color in gold of inferior color is quite clear.
Now he states the definition of <s>cullikā</s> with the phrase "from <s>pataṅgī</s> paste."

children.text: pataṅgī aśuddharasoparasādikṛtabījajīrṇaḥ pāradastadghaṭito yaḥ kalkastena jātaṃ yallohe tāmrādau gauravatejasvitvādiguṇasahitaṃ tāratvaṃ hematā vā kiṃcitkālaparyantaṃ sthitvā naśyati sā kriyā culliketi matā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pataṅgī</s> is mercury that has digested a seed made from impure <s>rasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, and the like. The operation by which, from a paste compounded with that, the silver-nature or gold-nature produced in a metal such as copper, along with qualities such as heaviness and brilliance, disappears after remaining for some time, is considered <s>cullikā</s>.
And it is said in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>:

children.text: yaḥ punaretaiḥ kurute karmāśuddhair bhaved rasastasya
children.translated_text: But the mercury of a person who performs the operation with these when they are impure

children.text: avyāpakaḥ pataṅgī na rase rasāyane yojyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes non-pervasive, a <s>pataṅgī</s>; it is not to be used in mercury elixirs.
Thus it says.
"With these" means with <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s.
"Operation" means an operation such as digestion.
<s>Pataṅgī</s> means one that goes upward like a bird.
The paste compounded with mercury should be understood as that taught in works such as the <s>Yogataraṅgiṇī</s>.
Accordingly it is said in the <s>Taraṅgiṇī</s>:
For one eight-<s>ṭaṅka</s> measure of mercury, two <s>pala</s>s of yellow calamine
should be ground very firmly until the mercury dissolves.
Then, together with citron juice and molasses,

children.text: śoṣayeccātape piṣṭvā ślakṣṇaṃ kṛtvā ca dhāryate ||
children.translated_text: one should dry it in the sun after grinding it, make it fine, and keep it.
Levigation with the latex of <s>arka</s> should be given to it again and again.

children.text: asya kalkasya siddhasya bhāga ekaśca ṭaṅkaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of this prepared paste, one part, and borax,
having added three parts of copper, should be blown in a closed crucible.
It will become gold with divine brilliance, surpassing saffron.
Thus it says.
In the same way, in works such as those of <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, a paste that produces silver-nature should also be examined.

children.text: saṃprati kriyāviśeṣasiddhasyāciravināśino lohasthasya rāgasya saṃjñāmāha rañjitāditi ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the technical name for the color present in a metal, produced by a special operation, which is not destroyed immediately, with the phrase "from what has been colored."
Here too, the phrase "from <s>pataṅgī</s> paste" is to be carried forward.

children.text: tādṛśakalkena rañjitāllohāddhmānādiyatnena vinā kālāntare dhmānena sadyo vā yo rāgo viniryāti viyujya nirgacchati sa pataṅgīrāgasaṃjñako rasaśāstre khyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The color that, from a metal colored by such a paste, comes out, that is, separates and emerges, either later by blowing without effort such as blowing and the like, or immediately by blowing, is known in <s>rasaśāstra</s> by the name <s>pataṅgī-rāga</s>.
The word is "melted."
An example of this is as follows:
Ash of <s>suradāli</s>, melted twenty-one times, then dried with cow-water,
by sprinkling makes sharp iron placed in a crucible like water.
Thus it says.
Likewise:
Dust from the body of <s>suragopaka</s> should be added with equal parts of <s>suradāli</s> fruits;
when sprinkled into melted gold, it at once remains fluid, resembling mercury.
Thus it says.
"Resembling mercury" means like water.
Now he states in order the definition of the eighteen saṃskāras with the word "with alkalis and acids."
The alkalis are barley-alkali, <s>sarjana</s>-alkali, and borax.
Acid means sour gruel and the like.
The medicines are such things as <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> and such plants as <s>sarpākṣī</s>.
These have indeed been enumerated in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s> in the procedure for sour gruel used for sweating and the other operations.
And that work says:
With various grains, as available, freed from husks and mixed with water,

children.text: mṛdbhāṇḍe pūritaṃ rakṣa yāvad amlatvam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: one should fill an earthen pot and keep it until it becomes sour.
In it, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,

children.text: triphalā girikarṇī ca haṃsapādī ca citrakam
children.translated_text: <s>triphalā</s>, <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
having pounded them together with their roots, one should add them as available.
In the pot of previous acid, this is called grain-acid.
It should be used everywhere for <s>rasarāja</s>, in sweating and the other operations.
Thus it says.
The meaning is: mercury that has been placed inside a packet of birch bark wrapped in cloth smeared with a paste of <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> and the like.
The paste of <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> and the like is also described in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s>, salt, mustard, turmeric, liquid <s>triphalā</s>,
<s>mahābalā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgī citrakaṃ ca navasāraṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and sal ammoniac, each in equal measure:

children.text: etat samastaṃ vyastaṃ vā pūrvāmlenaiva peṣayet ||
children.translated_text: all these together or separately should be ground with the previous acid alone.
With that paste one should smear the cloth to the thickness of a finger.

children.text: tanmadhye nikṣipet sūtaṃ baddhvā pacyād dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: One should place mercury in the midst of that, bind it up, and cook it for three days.
Mercury becomes sweated in a swing-apparatus joined with acid liquid.
After washing it with warm sour gruel, one should take it and triturate it.
Thus.
It causes looseness of the impurities; and the impurities are the twelve defects.
That is, it produces looseness in them.

children.text: śithilānām eva hi teṣām mocayitum śakyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For only when they have been loosened is it possible to remove them.

children.text: dvādaśa doṣāśca viṣaṃ vahnir malaśceti naisargikāstrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the twelve defects are three natural ones: poison, fire, and impurity.
One is born from lead.
One is born from tin.
Likewise there are those born from earth, from mountain, and from water.
There are two born from lead.
And two born from tin.

children.text: iti sapta kañcukākhyā ityevaṃ dvādaśa doṣā devaiḥ prārthitamaheśvareṇa pārade saṃyojitā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus the seven called sheaths, in this way the twelve defects, were joined to mercury by <s>Maheśvara</s> when he was entreated by the gods.
With the word 'stated'.

By the medicines beginning with house-soot, taught in the procedure of trituration to be stated later, and by all acids, the substances beginning with sour vetasa that are mentioned in the acid group.
The meaning is: by their juice.

children.text: tathā kāñjikairapi pāradasya yatpeṣaṇaṃ tridinaparyantaṃ kṛtaṃ tad bahirmalavināśanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the trituration of mercury with sour gruel too, when performed for three days, destroys the external impurity.

children.text: bahirmalaḥ svedenāntarviśliṣṭo bhūtvā pāradadehādbahiḥ saṃśliṣṭo rāgato naisargikadoṣaṃ vihāya navavidho yo malastadvināśako bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: The external impurity, having been loosened inwardly by sweating, adheres outwardly to the body of the mercury; apart from the natural defect caused by color, the ninefold impurity is what it destroys. This is the meaning.

children.text: kevalaṃ svedamardanābhyāṃ na sarvathā bhujakañcukadoṣanāśanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By sweating and trituration alone, the destruction of the serpent-sheath defects is not complete in every respect.

children.text: ato mardanapūrvakam agniyogena nāśaṃ kṛtvā pāradasya yat piṣṭatvotpādanaṃ tanmūrchanasaṃskāranāmnāha mardanādiṣṭeti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the production of a powdered state in mercury, after destroying them by the application of fire preceded by trituration, is called by the name of the mūrchana-saṃskāra; he states this with 'beginning with trituration'.

children.text: mardanārthaṃ vakṣyamāṇamūrchanasaṃskāravidhau kathitair gṛhakanyādibhir naṣṭapiṣṭatvakārakaṃ yat karma mardanapūrvakapācanarūpaṃ tanmūrchanam ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of trituration, the operation that produces the lost powdered state by means of house-aloe and the other substances taught in the mūrchana-saṃskāra procedure to be stated later, and that has the form of cooking preceded by trituration, is called mūrchana.

children.text: samāsato lakṣaṇaṃ tu dattagrāsasya grāsarahitasya vā gālanapātanavyaktirekeṇa pūrvāvasthāpannatvam ||
children.translated_text: In brief, its definition is the attainment of the previous condition, whether it has been given a morsel or has no morsel, except for the manifestation of melting and falling.

children.text: tacca mardanapākābhyāṃ bhavatīti mardanottaraṃ yantrapuṭānyatareṇa pāko'pyaṅgatvena bodhya iti dvau yaugikau ||
children.translated_text: And that occurs through trituration and cooking; therefore, after trituration, cooking by one or another apparatus-heating should also be understood as an accessory. Thus there are two combined procedures.
By the word bhūja, one should understand the earth-born defect and the others.

children.text: te ca kañcukā āvarakāḥ sapta doṣā vaṅgāhidoṣapramukhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those sheaths, the enclosing seven defects, are the ones beginning with the tin and serpent defects.
And they are destroyed by trituration and fire.
By the word tin, the tin-born defect is to be understood.
And by the word serpent, the lead-born defect is meant.

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ nānātvena vividhadṛḍhaśithilasaṃsargatāratamyena tannāśārthaṃ vividhopāyapradarśanam ucitam eveti na mardanasaṃskāreṇa mūrchanasya gatārthateti śaṅkyamiti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the defects are diverse, and because there are gradations of various firm and loose conjunctions, it is indeed proper to show various methods for their destruction. Thus one should not object that mūrchana is already accomplished by the trituration-saṃskāra alone; this is the purport.

children.text: tanmūrchanaṃ hi vaṅgāhibhūjakañcukanāśanam iti pāṭhaṃ gṛhītveyaṃ vyākhyā ||
children.translated_text: This explanation accepts the reading: 'that mūrchana destroys the tin, serpent, earth-born, and sheath defects.'

children.text: doṣatrayavināśanamiti pāṭhe tu naisargikadoṣanāśe sutarāṃ bahirdoṣanāśa ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But under the reading 'it destroys the three defects,' the intended meaning is that, when the natural defects are destroyed, the external defects are all the more destroyed.

children.text: ata evāyaṃ pāṭho rasahṛdayaṭīkāyāṃ caturbhujamiśritair ādṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason this reading was accepted by <s>Caturbhuja Miśra</s> in the commentary on the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>.

children.text: naisargikadoṣetaradoṣāṇāṃ vāraṇāya pūrvoktamardanasaṃskāro naisargikadoṣavāraṇāyāyam iti vyavasthāyāḥ sukaratvāt ||
children.translated_text: For it is easy to establish that the trituration-saṃskāra mentioned earlier prevents defects other than the natural defects, while this one prevents the natural defects.

children.text: evaṃ ca vaṅgāhibhūjakañcukanāśanam iti pāṭho na manorama iti bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should understand that the reading 'destroying the tin, serpent, earth-born, and sheath defects' is not pleasing.
With the word 'sweating'.
Sweating is the steaming, in a swing-apparatus, with sour gruel, alkalis, acids, and salts.
Application of sunlight is keeping mercury that has been triturated with sour gruel and the like in a glass vessel placed in the heat of the sun.

children.text: ādiśabdena sāgnikacullīsthe kaṭāhe vā pāradasya tasya dhāraṇamityādi ||
children.translated_text: By the word 'and so on' is meant, for example, keeping that mercury in a pan placed on a fire-heated stove.

children.text: tena pāradasya mūrchitasya yaccāñcalyatejasvitvagauravaviśiṣṭatvarūpam ātmarūpaṃ tatpratiprāpaṇaṃ tadutthāpanam ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: By that, the restoration of the essential form of stupefied mercury, consisting in mobility, brilliance, and heaviness, is called utthāpana.
Now he states the definition of the pātana-saṃskāra with the words 'with the stated medicines'.

children.text: vakṣyamāṇapātanavidhau nirdiṣṭatriphalādibheṣajaiḥ saha marditapāradasya tata ūrdhvapātanādiyantrasthitasya yanniryāpaṇam ūrdhvādhastiryakprāpaṇaṃ tat pātanam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The expulsion of mercury that has been triturated together with the medicines beginning with triphalā, specified in the pātana procedure to be stated later, and then placed in apparatuses for upward pātana and the like, namely its conveyance upward, downward, or sideways, is called pātana.

children.text: tena vaṅganāgajā yaugikadoṣā bhūjādisaptakañcukāśca sarvathā naśyanti ||
children.translated_text: By it the combined defects born from tin and lead and the seven sheaths beginning with earth-born defects are completely destroyed.
He defines rodhana with the word 'water'.
In a pot means in the jar-apparatus to be described later.
Āpyāyanī means nourishing.

children.text: atra saindhavamayamūṣāsaṃpuṭitaṃ kṛtvaikaviṃśatidinaparyantaṃ bhūdharapuṭanaṃ sṛṣṭyambujaiḥ saha mardanaṃ ca kṛtvā tataḥ param iti vākyaśeṣo bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the remainder of the sentence should be understood as: after enclosing it in a crucible made of rock salt, applying a bhūdhara-heating for twenty-one days, and triturating it with the waters of creation, then afterward.
The phrase to be supplied is: 'of mercury that has obtained potency'.

children.text: svedaḥ pāradagarbhitamūṣāṃ bhūmimadhye gūḍhāṃ kṛtvā bhūmyupari karīṣāgnir ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sweating here means that a crucible containing mercury is buried in the ground, and a fire of cow-dung cakes is placed on top of the ground.
Now he defines the dīpana-saṃskāra with the phrase 'metals and stones'.
Metals are copper sheets and the like.
Stones are crystal, blue vitriol, green vitriol, and the like.
Roots are roots such as sarpākṣī.
By the word 'and so on', alkalis, salts, water, and the like are to be understood.

children.text: ghaṭamadhyago ghaṭayantramadhyagaḥ pāradastridinaparyantaṃ svedyo bhavati yasmin karmaṇi tad dīpanam iti khyātam ||
children.translated_text: In the operation in which mercury, being inside the pot, that is, inside the pot-apparatus, is steamed for three days, that is known as <s>dīpana</s>.

children.text: atha jāraṇāyām ayathābalam ayathākramaṃ ca grāsadānenājīrṇadoṣāt pārade vikriyā syād iti grāsamānavicāro'vaśyaṃ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, in <s>jāraṇā</s>, if the morsel is given without regard to capacity and without regard to sequence, a disturbance may arise in the mercury because of the fault of indigestion; therefore an examination of the measure of the morsel must necessarily be made.
Therefore he states the definition of the process called the measure of the morsel, with the words "of such a measure".
Here the word "such" denotes a particular measure, such as a pala, of the mercury that is to be processed.

children.text: tādṛśamānamitapāradasyeyaccatuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśādimitābhrakasattvabījādyātmakaṃ dravyaṃ bhakṣaṇāya dattaṃ cet sukhena cīrṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ ca syāditi niścitā yā bījāder mitis tadgrāsamānaṃ khyātam ||
children.translated_text: If a substance consisting of mica-essence, seed, and the like, measured as one sixty-fourth part and so on of mercury measured in that way, is given for consumption and is certainly digested and assimilated easily, then the measured quantity of seed and the like is known as the measure of the morsel.

children.text: atha jāraṇāṃ lilakṣayiṣuḥ prathamaṃ sādhāraṇāṃstadavasthābhedān salakṣaṇān samāsata āha grāsasyeti ||
children.translated_text: Now, wishing to define <s>jāraṇā</s>, he first briefly states its common subdivisions, with their definitions, with the words "of the morsel".

children.text: śreṣṭhai rasavārttākuśalaiḥ sarvavidhā jāraṇā trirūpā triprakārā kathitā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By the best experts in the lore of mercury, every kind of <s>jāraṇā</s> is said to have three forms, three types.
Among these, the carrying-in of the morsel is the act of making the morsel be eaten by mercury.
The melting in the womb is the liquefaction, inside the belly of the mercury, of the swallowed seed and the like.
And <s>jāraṇā</s> is the unification with mercury through an endless firm connection.
He will state the definitions of these immediately afterward.

children.text: punarapi jāraṇāyā avasthākṛtanāmāntarāṇi trīṇyāha grāsaḥ piṣṭiḥ parīṇāmaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Again he states three other names of <s>jāraṇā</s> based on its states: morsel, paste, and transformation.
Among these, the morsel is swallowing.

children.text: piṣṭiḥ svedanamardanāgnyādibhiḥ pāradodare drutagrāsasya pāradasahitasya śuṣkaścūrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The paste is the dry powder of the morsel melted in the belly of mercury and joined with the mercury, produced by steaming, rubbing, fire, and the like.
The meaning of transformation is just as stated before.
Again, <s>jāraṇā</s> is of two kinds.
They are distinguished as with a mouth and without a mouth.

children.text: tatrālpavaktavyatvāt prathamaṃ nirmukhāyā eva lakṣaṇamāha nirmukheti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, because there is little to say, he first states the definition of the mouthless one, with the word "mouthless".

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭibhāgamitaṃ bījaṃ prathamaṃ yatra pāradodare na dīyate kiṃtu kevalaṃ śuddhadhātvādigrāsa eva sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇāvāsanauṣadhimardanādyupāyair jāryate sā jāraṇā nirmukhetyucyate ||
children.translated_text: Where seed measuring one sixty-fourth part is not first placed in the belly of mercury, but rather only a morsel of purified metal and the like is digested by means such as the three creations, water-particles, impregnation, medicinal rubbing, and so forth, that <s>jāraṇā</s> is called mouthless.
Its use should be made in the <s>jāraṇā</s> of soft substances such as <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s.
He states the meaning of the word <s>bīja</s>, which is useful for making a mouth, with the word "pure".

children.text: śuddham akṛtrimam uttamaṃ khanijaṃ svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ vaitacchāstroktaśuddhyā suśuddhaṃ kṛtvātra grāhyam ||
