children.translated_text: Here pure, non-artificial, excellent mineral gold and silver, made thoroughly pure by the purification taught in this very science, should be accepted.
By this, artificial, extracted, great seed and the like are excluded.

children.text: uktabījasya yathākramaṃ svarṇotpādārthaṃ raupyajananārthaṃ ca pāradasya catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśena pāradodare jāraṇārambhe prakṣepaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of producing gold and generating silver, respectively, the aforesaid seed should be placed in the belly of mercury at the beginning of <s>jāraṇā</s>, in the amount of one sixty-fourth part of the mercury.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte tasmin bīje pāradodare yathāvidhi cīrṇe jīrṇe ca sati pāradaḥ satvaraṃ grāsabhakṣaṇaṃ karotīti śāstre sa raso mukhavānityucyate ||
children.translated_text: When this is done, and when that seed in the belly of the mercury has been digested and assimilated according to rule, the mercury quickly eats the morsel; therefore that mercury is called "possessed of a mouth" in the science.

children.text: tatkṛtaṃ yat kaṭhinalohādibhakṣaṇaṃ sā jāraṇā samukhetyuktā ||
children.translated_text: The eating of hard metals and the like produced by that is called <s>jāraṇā</s> with a mouth.

children.text: mṛgacāriṇā mṛgasahitaṃ vane carati saṃsāraṃ vihāya viriktena kenacidvaravārtikena ||
children.translated_text: By one who wanders like a deer, together with deer, in the forest, having abandoned worldly life, by some excellent detached instructor.
Now he states the definition of mercury with a great mouth, with the word "divine herbs".
The sixty-four divine herbs, such as <s>somalatā</s>, and conjunction with them: mercury processed by rubbing and the like with their juice.

children.text: tena prakāśamūṣāsvapi sthito'gnisahaḥ pārado dhmānena kaṭhinaṃ mṛdu sarvaṃ lohādi yadā bhunakti asau mahāmukhavān ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: When mercury, even while placed in open crucibles, withstands fire and, through blowing, consumes everything hard and soft, metal and the like, it is called possessed of a great mouth.
He states the definitions of the previously mentioned carrying-in and so on, with the word "of mercury".
"Having melted it outside".
The liquefaction of mica-essence has already been stated before, in the second chapter.
The rest of the sentence is: "it is placed inside a heated mortar for <s>jāraṇā</s>."
Now he states the definition of <s>jāraṇā</s>, with the words "of the melted morsel".

children.text: biḍayantrādiyogena pāradodare dravībhūtasya grāsasya bījāder yaḥ parīṇāmo'vināśidṛḍhatarasaṃbandhena pāradena sahaikībhāvaḥ sā jāraṇetyucyate ||
children.translated_text: The transformation of a morsel, such as seed, that has become liquid inside the belly of mercury through the use of the <s>biḍa</s>-apparatus and the like, namely its unification with mercury by means of an indestructible and very firm connection, is called <s>jāraṇā</s>.
Its types are countless, very many.
This is because apparatuses and the like are of many kinds.

children.text: te ca prakārāḥ patrajāraṇāsattvajāraṇādrutijāraṇābījajāraṇāmahābījajāraṇāsiddhabījajāraṇāsadhūmajāraṇānirdhūmajāraṇābālajāraṇāvṛddhajāraṇābaddhajāraṇābhūcarījāraṇākhecarījāraṇāprabhṛtayo rasārṇavādau savistaraṃ bodhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those types, such as leaf-<s>jāraṇā</s>, essence-<s>jāraṇā</s>, liquid-<s>jāraṇā</s>, seed-<s>jāraṇā</s>, great-seed-<s>jāraṇā</s>, perfected-seed-<s>jāraṇā</s>, smoky <s>jāraṇā</s>, smokeless <s>jāraṇā</s>, young <s>jāraṇā</s>, old <s>jāraṇā</s>, bound <s>jāraṇā</s>, earth-moving <s>jāraṇā</s>, sky-moving <s>jāraṇā</s>, and so forth, should be understood in detail from the <s>Rasārṇava</s> and other works.

One should know the swing apparatus, the soma-fire apparatus, the wheel-king apparatus, the sand apparatus, the water-tortoise apparatus, the ground-tortoise apparatus, crucibles, and so forth as apparatuses for <s>jāraṇā</s>.

children.text: taptakhalve mardanaṃ tu sarvatra prākkāryam eva ||
children.translated_text: But rubbing in a heated mortar must always be done first everywhere.
By the word "and so forth" are included procedures such as rubbing together with six drops and worms, and the three creations.
Therefore, after the <s>jāraṇā</s> of mica leaves, he defines the coloring process with the words "well-perfected seed".

children.text: susiddhaṃ yathāvidhi sādhitaṃ yad bījam abhrakasattvadhātvādicūrṇaṃ tajjāraṇena pāradasya yā bījadhātvādyanurūpā varṇotpattis tad rañjanam ||
children.translated_text: The seed that is well perfected, prepared according to rule, namely powder of mica-essence, metals, and the like: through the <s>jāraṇā</s> of that, the production in mercury of a color corresponding to the seed, metal, and the like is called coloring.
There, however, the method for preparing the seed has already been stated above in the explanation of the characteristics of perfected seed.
The method of <s>jāraṇā</s> will become clear in the thirtieth chapter.
The word 'and so on' includes gems, <s>rasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, and the like.
The example of coloring substances and the procedure are found in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>.
As follows:
Mercury in which mica has been digested displays a shade corresponding to the mica:

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ raktāṃ pītāṃ sītāṃ tathā saṃkarairmiśrām ||
children.translated_text: black, red, yellow, white, and likewise mixed through combinations.
Likewise:

children.text: krāmati tīkṣṇena rasastīkṣṇena ca jīryate kṣaṇādgrāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury moves by means of sharp metal, and the morsel is digested in an instant by sharp metal.
Sharp metal is the womb of gold; by means of sharp metal it takes on colors.

children.text: tadapi ca daradena hataṃ hatvā vā mākṣikeṇa ravisahitam
children.translated_text: And that too, struck by cinnabar, or after striking it with pyrite together with copper,

children.text: vāsitamapi vāsanayā ghanavaccāryaṃ ca jāryaṃ ca
children.translated_text: even when impregnated by impregnation, is to be made to consume and is to be digested like mica.
'Impregnated by impregnation' means treated, that is, repeatedly processed, with an impregnating medicine.
Likewise:

children.text: kāntaṃ vā tīkṣṇaṃ vā kāñcīṃ vā vajrasasyakādīnām
children.translated_text: Lodestone, or sharp metal, or kāñcī, or one among diamond, sasyaka, and the rest,
or all of them: even a mixture is desired in the coloring of mercury.
Kāñcī means gold pyrite.
By the word 'and the rest', diamond, capala, and other secondary metals, even when combined together, are also intended.

children.text: kuṭile balamadhikaṃ rāgastīkṣṇe tu pannage snehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In crooked metal there is greater strength; in sharp metal there is coloring; but in nāga there is adhesiveness.
Those who know metals declare that coloring, adhesiveness, and strength are found in kamala.
He states the definition of <s>sāraṇā</s> with the word 'sūta'.

children.text: sāraṇākhyatailenārdhāṃśaṃ saṃbhṛtaṃ yat sāraṇāyantraṃ tatra sthite pārade yat svarṇādikṣepaṇaṃ svarṇādibījanāgavaṅgānāṃ yat kṣepaṇaṃ vedhādhikyasiddhyarthaṃ kriyate sā sāraṇeti rasaśāstra uktā ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus, filled to the half with the oil called <s>sāraṇā</s> oil, the placing of gold and the like into mercury that is situated there, that is, the insertion of gold and other seeds, nāga, and vaṅga, performed for the accomplishment of a greater <s>vedha</s>, is called <s>sāraṇā</s> in rasaśāstra.
Its two varieties are called <s>pratisāraṇā</s> and <s>anusāraṇā</s>.
And this has been stated in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>:
Mercury that has been made to move, when it combines with an equal amount of seed, is to be called <s>sārya</s>.
With twice the amount it is <s>pratīsārya</s>, and with three times the amount it is <s>anusārya</s>.
Thus.
Even the double amount is gold alone.
Greater <s>vedha</s> means penetration: it breaks through and enters within; this becomes increased.

children.text: pāradasya tāmradalādau śarīrasthadhātvādiṣu ca sarvato vyāptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is the complete pervasion of mercury in copper leaves and the like, and also in the bodily metals and so forth.
The <s>sāraṇā</s> oil has already been stated above in the explanation of the fifth chapter.
In the chapter on apparatuses, the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus and the method of <s>sāraṇā</s> will become clear.

children.text: atha krāmaṇasya dravyasya sarvadā vedhasahopayogitvena samāsato viśeṣaṇamukhena krāmaṇalakṣaṇasahitaṃ vedhalakṣaṇam ekena ślokenāha vyavāyīti ||
children.translated_text: Now, because the substance for <s>krāmaṇa</s> is always used together with <s>vedha</s>, he briefly states, by way of qualification, the definition of <s>vedha</s> together with the definition of <s>krāmaṇa</s> in a single verse, with the word 'vyavāyi'.

children.text: dravye śatavedhādau yathābhāgaṃ gṛhīte mūṣāyāṃ drute kṛte prataptamātre vā tāmrarajatādau sādhyadravye kṣipto rasaḥ pārado yasmin karmaṇi sa vedha ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: In an operation where mercury is thrown into a substance to be accomplished, such as copper or silver, when a substance such as one for hundredfold <s>vedha</s> has been taken in the proper proportion and melted in a crucible, or when it has merely been heated, that operation is called <s>vedha</s>.
And what sort of mercury is that?
It is furnished with a <s>vyavāyi</s> medicine.

children.text: yat sevitamātraṃ tatkṣaṇa eva śarīrāntaḥsthasarvadhātuṣu sahasā sabāhyābhyantaraṃ vyāpnoti paścāt pākaṃ prāpnoti tadvyavāyi krāmaṇetyaparaparyāyaṃ ca bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: A thing which, as soon as it is consumed, immediately and suddenly pervades all the internal bodily constituents, both externally and internally, and afterward undergoes digestion, is called <s>vyavāyi</s>; it should also be understood as having <s>krāmaṇa</s> as another synonym.

children.text: tādṛśabheṣajopeto yogavāhī pārado'pi sevitaścet sahasā sarvaṃ dehaṃ sāntaraṃ vyāpnoti na kevalaṃ koṣṭha eva sthitiṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: If mercury, which is a carrier of the formulation and is furnished with such a medicine, is consumed, it too suddenly pervades the whole body internally; it does not remain only in the stomach.

children.text: na vā dhātuṣu kathaṃcit prāpto'pi bahiḥ saṃlagna eva tiṣṭhatīti ||
children.translated_text: Nor, even if it somehow reaches the bodily constituents, does it remain merely attached on the outside.
The combination of substances by which mercury enters inside metal
is immediately called <s>krāmaṇa</s>, giver of success in mercury.
Thus it should be understood as distinct from the definition of <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
Now he states the varieties of <s>vedha</s>, with the word 'lepa'.
'By smearing'.

children.text: yasminvedhe pārado lepena lohaṃ pattrīkṛtaṃ tīkṣṇatāmrādi svarṇaṃ karoti rajataṃ vā karoti sa lepavedha ityuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>vedha</s> in which mercury, by smearing, turns metal beaten into leaf, such as sharp metal or copper, into gold or turns it into silver, that is called <s>lepavedha</s>.

children.text: atra lepottaraṃ varṇotkarṣārthaṃ yat puṭaṃ deyaṃ bhavati tat puṭaṃ saukaraṃ varāhapuṭaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Here, after the smearing, the heating that must be given for the sake of improving the color should be a <s>saukara</s> heating, that is, a boar-heating.

children.text: asmin saṃskāre jīrṇacaturthāṃśārdhāṃśasamādibhāgair jīrṇabīja eva sārito rasa upayoktavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this operation, mercury made to undergo <s>sāraṇā</s> only with seed digested in one-fourth, one-half, equal, and similar proportions should be used.
Now he states <s>kṣepavedha</s>, with the word 'throwing in'.

children.text: dhmānena mūṣāyāṃ lohe tāmrādau drute sati krāmaṇadravyakalkasahitasya pāradasya yat prakṣepaṇaṃ sa vedhaḥ kṣepa iti khyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When metal such as copper has been melted in a crucible by blowing, the throwing in of mercury together with a paste of <s>krāmaṇa</s> substances is the <s>vedha</s> known as <s>kṣepa</s>.

children.text: atra pakṣāntaram apyuktaṃ rasasāre krāmaṇakalkasahitalohe dhāmyamāne kevalaṃ pāradaṃ kṣipettatreti ||
children.translated_text: Here another view is also stated in the <s>Rasasāra</s>: when metal together with <s>krāmaṇa</s> paste is being blown, one should throw in mercury alone there.
He states the definition of <s>dhūmavedha</s> with the word 'in the fire'.

children.text: dhūmāyamāne vahnāvantarmūṣāntaḥsthatadvahnimadhye prakṣipto yo rasaḥ pāradas tatsaṃbandhidhūmasyordhvasthāpitatāmrādipatre saṃparkād yat svarṇarajatāpādanaṃ sa dhūmavedha ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: When mercury is cast into a smoking fire, inside the crucible, in the midst of that fire, and through contact of the smoke connected with it with a copper or similar leaf placed above there is production of gold or silver, that is called <s>dhūmavedha</s>.

children.text: sūtena sabāhyābhyantaravyāptyaikībhūtasya siddhadravyasya suvarṇatvādiprāptasya tāmrādilohātmakadravyasya tadekībhūtasūtasya ca yathāsambhavaṃ yat kāluṣyādi tannivārakaṃ daśāṃśena yaccūrṇaprakṣepādi karma tad udghāṭanam itīritam ||
children.translated_text: For a perfected substance that has become unified with mercury through external and internal pervasion and has attained the state of gold and the like, namely a substance made of copper or another metal, and also for the mercury unified with it, the operation of adding powder and the like in a tenth part, which removes, as appropriate, blackness and similar defects, is called <s>udghāṭana</s>.
Blackness means being mixed with impurity.
By the word "and so on" one should include defects such as having an umbrella-like form, having moth-like behavior, being hard to melt, being hard to combine, and the like.

children.text: sāraṇottaraṃ rasāyanaṃ kartuṃ kāmayamānena sādhakena pāradasya kartavyau svedasaṃnyāsākhyasaṃskārau lakṣayati kṣārāmlairiti ||
children.translated_text: For the practitioner who wishes, after <s>sāraṇā</s>, to perform <s>rasāyana</s>, he defines the two <s>saṃskāra</s>s of mercury called steaming and <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, with the words "with alkalis and acids."

children.text: auṣadhair bhṛṅgarāṅmuṇḍī viṣṇukrāntā ityādibhiḥ svedalakṣaṇavarṇanāvasare prāguktaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With medicines such as <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and others, which were previously mentioned when the definition of steaming was being described.

children.text: taiśca sārdhaṃ saha pāradaṃ bhāṇḍamadhye pidhānasaṃdhirodhanādiyatnena ruddhvā tadbhāṇḍaṃ bhūmimadhye nikhanyate yasmin karmaṇi tat svedanaṃ saṃprakīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Together with those, mercury is shut inside a vessel by the effort of sealing the joint of the lid and so on, and that vessel is buried in the ground; the operation in which this is done is called steaming.

children.text: athauṣadhayuktasya pāradasya mṛnmayabhāṇḍasaṃpuṭitasya mandavahniyuktacullīmadhye kṣiptvā yat puṭanaṃ sa saṃnyāsa ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, when mercury mixed with medicines and enclosed in a clay vessel is put into a stove furnished with a gentle fire and baked, that is called <s>saṃnyāsa</s>.
Now, for the slight steaming of very soft substances such as leaves and flowers, he states another apparatus, with the words "a water-containing pot."

children.text: sthālīṃ caturthāṃśajalena pūritodarāṃ jalenārdhapūritodarāṃ vā kṛtvā tasyā mukham ā samantād vastreṇa baddhaṃ yathā syāttathā mukhābaddhe vastre pākyaṃ svedyam atikomalaṃ dravyaṃ vinikṣipya nyubjaśarāvādinā pidhāyācchādya yatra pacyate tat svedanīyantramityucyate ||
children.translated_text: A pot is made with its interior filled with one quarter water, or with its interior half-filled with water; its mouth is tied all around with cloth, and the very delicate substance to be cooked or steamed is placed on the cloth tied over the mouth. Where it is cooked after being covered with an inverted bowl or the like, that is called a steaming apparatus.
He will call this very apparatus by the name "ball."
Now he describes the upward-sublimation apparatus, with the words "eight fingers."

children.text: atha nyubjasthāpyasya viśālapṛṣṭhasya mṛtpātrasyāṅgulād adho 'ṅgulamitapṛṣṭhabhāgād adhobhāge toyādhāraḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, below the broad back of the clay vessel that is to be placed upside down, below the part of the back measuring one finger from the edge, a water-reservoir should be made.
How?
In such a way that it has a circumference of eight fingers and an inner breadth of eight fingers.

children.text: tathānāhena bandhena saha daśāṅgulaṃ yathā syāttathā bandha ālavālaṃ tatpradeśaṃ saṃgṛhya daśāṅgulavistāram ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, together with the breadth and the rim, it should be ten fingers; the rim, taking in the surrounding channel-region, is ten fingers broad. This is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ ca bandhasthaulyam aṅguladvayamitaṃ garbhavistāraścāṣṭāṅgulamitaḥ kārya ityavatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is established that the thickness of the rim should measure two fingers, and the inner breadth should measure eight fingers.
The reading is not "in the binding."

children.text: caturaṅgulocchrāyaṃ yathā syāttathā toyādhāraḥ pṛṣṭhe kārya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the water-reservoir should be made on the back so as to be four fingers high.
The mouth of the lower vessel should be inserted beneath the opening of that upper vessel, whose back is sixteen fingers broad and is furnished with such a support.
Then one should smear the joint at the sides of the mouth with buffalo milk and the like and let it dry.
The powder is lime, that is, a white substance for plastering.
It is declared to be a sublimation apparatus.
The meaning is that the upward-sublimation apparatus has been stated.
He describes the downward-sublimation apparatus, with the words "above this."

children.text: jalādhāravihīnasya vaiparītyena jale sthāpitasyāsyoktayantrasya saṃbandhi yad ūrdhvabhājanaṃ tatra liptasthāpitasya lepaṃ kṛtvā sthāpitasya pāradasya yantropari dīptairvanopalairadhaḥpātaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In the upper vessel belonging to this same apparatus, which lacks the water-reservoir and is placed in water in the reverse arrangement, mercury is set after being smeared or after a coating has been applied; then, with blazing forest-cakes placed above the apparatus, one should make it descend downward.
This has been stated as the downward-sublimation apparatus.
The tortoise apparatus is of two kinds: the water-tortoise and the ground-tortoise.
Of these, he now describes the water-tortoise, with the words "filled with water."

children.text: ghaṭakharparaṃ khaṇḍitamukhaṃ sacchidraṃ ghaṭakhaṇḍamuttānaṃ dattvā tadupari koṣṭhīṃ mūṣāṃ chidre kiṃcitpraviṣṭabudhnāṃ nīrāviyoginīmuttānāṃ sudṛḍhaṃ niścalaṃ saṃsthāpya koṣṭhīmabhitaḥ kuḍyaṃ vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: One sets a potsherd, that is, a pot fragment with a broken mouth and a hole, facing upward. On top of it one firmly and immovably places a <s>koṣṭhī</s> crucible, facing upward, with its base entering a little into the hole and not separated from the water, and then one should make a wall around the <s>koṣṭhī</s>.

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ biḍaṃ tanmadhye pāradaṃ ca dattvā sa samyaksthāpyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After putting <s>biḍa</s> in the <s>koṣṭhī</s> and mercury in the middle of it, it should be properly set in place.

children.text: tato laghulohakaṭorikayā nyubjayā taṃ pāradaṃ koṣṭhyāmācchādya mṛtkarpaṭādinā saṃdhiṃ ruddhvā tadghaṭakharparam aṅgāraiḥ karīṣādimiśraiḥ pūrṇaṃ kuryāt pūrṇaṃ tad ghaṭakharparam aṅgāraiḥ karīṣatuṣamiśraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one covers that mercury in the <s>koṣṭhī</s> with a small iron bowl turned upside down, seals the joint with clay cloth and the like, and fills that potsherd with coals mixed with cow-dung and the like; that potsherd is filled with coals mixed with cow-dung and husks.
In place of "the embryos melt," the reading is "there is melting in the womb of all metals."

children.text: evaṃ rītyā kacchapayantrasthaḥ pāradaḥ svedanato vahnitāpena mardanato biḍādinā saha pākāvasare tatraiva jātena mardanena drutaṃ grāsaṃ tridinaṃ jarati ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, mercury situated in the tortoise apparatus, through steaming, through the heat of fire, and through rubbing together with <s>biḍa</s> and the like, at the time of cooking and by the rubbing produced there itself, quickly digests the morsel for three days.
Thus the sense is that this apparatus is useful for <s>jāraṇā</s> preceded by melting in the womb.

children.text: atra jalapūrṇapātraṃ bhūmāveva nikhātaṃ kṛtvā tanmukhe sacchidramuttānaṃ śarāvaṃ dattvā tatra chidre nīrāviyoginīṃ mūṣāṃ kācavilepitāṃ dhṛtvā tatra pāradasyādhastādupariṣṭācca gandhakaṃ dattvā pidhāyoparyupalāgninā gandhakaṃ jārayanti kecit ||
children.translated_text: Here some people bury the water-filled vessel in the ground itself, place on its mouth an upward-facing bowl with a hole, put in that hole a crucible not separated from the water and smeared with glass-paste, place sulfur below and above the mercury there, cover it, and digest the sulfur by a fire of cakes above.

children.text: kiṃcaitadghaṭakaśarāve chidrasaṃsthitāṃ pakvamūṣāṃ kṛtvā tasyāmaṣṭāṃśabiḍāvṛtaṃ pāradaṃ dhṛtvā lohapātryāṃ saṃruddhaṃ mudritaṃ ca kṛtvā taduparyaṣṭāṅgulamānāṃ vālukāṃ vinikṣipya haṭhāttadupari dhmānena dhmātaṃ tadgarbhasambhūtaṃ rasaṃ māyūrapittaliptaṃ kāñcanaṃ grāsayantīti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, in this pot-bowl they make a fired crucible situated in the hole, put in it mercury covered with one eighth part <s>biḍa</s>, enclose and seal it with an iron dish, throw sand measuring eight fingers above it, and heat it forcefully by blowing from above; they then make gold smeared with peacock bile consume the <s>rasa</s> produced inside it.

children.text: sthalakūrmayantraṃ tu kiṃcidgartāyukte bhūtale tathaiva ghaṭakharparaṃ nyubjaṃ nidhāya saṃdhilepādi kṛtvā tadupari sarvataḥ pārśvabhāge ca puṭaṃ dadyāditi ||
children.translated_text: As for the ground-tortoise apparatus, one should place an inverted potsherd or pot in the same way on a piece of ground furnished with a small pit, make sealing with clay and the like, and then apply a <s>puṭa</s> (heating) above it and on all sides around it.

children.text: tatra gartāyāṃ vanasūraṇādikandodare biḍaṃ tanmadhye sagrāsaṃ pāradaṃ dattvā tatkandaśakalenaivācchādya mṛtkarpaṭādināveṣṭya saṃśoṣya dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: There, in the pit, one should put <s>biḍa</s> inside the hollow of a bulb such as wild sūraṇa; in the middle of it one should place mercury together with its morsel, cover it with a piece of that very bulb, wrap it with clay-smeared cloth and the like, dry it, and keep it there.
And on the back one should apply continuous fire for three days.

children.text: antarāntarā kandaparivartanaṃ kāryaṃ yathā kando na dahyeta ||
children.translated_text: From time to time the bulb should be turned, so that the bulb is not burned.
In this way one should perform <s>jāraṇā</s> by means of the ground-tortoise apparatus.

children.text: kande dagdhaprāye sati anyatrānyatra kande pūrvavattaṃ pāradaṃ dhṛtvā pācayet ||
children.translated_text: When the bulb has become nearly burned, the mercury should be placed again and again in another bulb as before and cooked.
Now he states the lamp apparatus with the words 'the tortoise apparatus'.

children.text: jalapūrṇapātramadhye ghaṭakalaśamuttānaṃ nidhāya tatra koṣṭhīmakṛtvā tatsthāne mṛnmayapīṭhaṃ kṛtvā tatra dīpikāṃ nidhāya dīpaṃ prajvālya nāgasvarṇabījasahitaṃ gandhakamanaḥśilāharītālasahitaṃ ca pāradaṃ mardanena piṣṭīkṛtaṃ poṭalikāyāṃ baddhvā kacchapākāranyubjamṛtpātrodare tailamagnāṃ tāṃ poṭalīṃ dīpajvālopari yathā syāttathāvalambitāṃ baddhvā tannyubjaṃ pātraṃ nyubjaṃ nidhāya dīpoṣmaṇā nāgaṃ bhakṣayitvā pārado jalapātre'dhaḥ patati yasmin yantre taddīpikāyantramuktam ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of a vessel filled with water one should place a pot or jar upright; having made a fire-pit there, and having made a clay seat in that place, one should place a lamp there and kindle it. Mercury, made into paste by trituration together with lead, gold seed, sulphur, realgar, and orpiment, should be tied in a small bundle. That bundle, immersed in oil inside an inverted clay vessel shaped like a tortoise, should be fastened so that it hangs above the flame of the lamp; that inverted vessel is then placed upside down. By the heat of the lamp the mercury consumes the lead and falls down into the water-vessel. The apparatus in which this occurs is called the lamp apparatus.
Its use should be understood as being for the apparatus intended for the <s>jāraṇā</s> of lead.

children.text: tato jīrṇanāgaṃ pāradaṃ bhasmamūṣāyāṃ dhmānena viyuktaṃ nāgaṃ kṛtvā tasminrase sādhakāvarabījaṃ jārayantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made mercury with digested lead into separated lead by blowing in an ash-crucible, practitioners digest the excellent seed in that mercury.
'Situated in the lamp' means properly placed above the lamp.
Now he states the ḍhekī apparatus with the words 'from the neck of the vessel'.

children.text: adhaśchidra upakaṇṭhaṃ kṛte chidre jalagarbhitaṃ svāduśītajalagarbhitam ||
children.translated_text: 'With a lower hole': a hole is made near the neck; 'filled with water' means filled with sweet, cool water.

children.text: yuktadravyaiḥ śuddhiyogyaiḥ kāñjikādibhiḥ pātanopayogidravaiśca saha saṃyukto raso ghaṭe sacchidropakaṇṭhe vahnisthite mṛnmayaghaṭe pūrvaṃ vinikṣiptaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, combined with suitable substances, namely purifying agents such as sour gruel and liquids useful for distillation, should first be placed in an earthen pot that has a hole near the neck and is set on the fire.

children.text: bhājanaṃ sampuṭaghaṭakam adhobhājanam uṣṇaṃ yāvadbhaved ghaṭe tāvadagniḥ kārya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The vessel is the enclosing pot; the lower vessel is to be heated, meaning that fire should be maintained under the pot until it becomes hot.
'Placement of mercury' means the proper depositing or setting down of mercury.
In the <s>Rasasāra</s>, a degā apparatus equal to this apparatus is described:
Taking a large vessel furnished with a hole in its belly,

children.text: bhāṇḍe kācaghaṭīṃ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ chidre niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: one should put a glass jar into the vessel and fit its mouth into the hole.
At its mouth there should be a glass tube, and that tube should face downward.

children.text: ruddhvā tadā tayoḥ saṃdhimardhaṃ ca nālakaṃ dihet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing the joint of the two, one should also smear half of the tube.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ vālukayāpūrya tasya dvāraṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Having filled the vessel with sand and closed its opening,
one should kindle the fire until that tube melts.
Then, after removing the cooled apparatus, one should wash the jar.
Having put in liquid again, one should apply it again; cooking is performed once more.
Thus, in the degā apparatus, an excellent liquefaction of tin is taught.

children.text: tālo nāgaḥ śilācauraḥ śulvo haṃsaśca gandhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Orpiment, lead, realgar, copper, haṃsa, and sulphur,

children.text: ete raṅgaṃ vimuñcanti vidrumaṃ gairikaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: these release tin, and so do coral and red ochre.
By means of the sand degā apparatus, piccha and keśa also melt.
Thus.
He states the vidyādhara apparatus.

children.text: tatra prathamaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ samāsata uktvānantaraṃ savistaramāha yantramiti ||
children.translated_text: There, first he states its form briefly, and afterward he explains it in detail with the word 'apparatus'.
'From the enclosure of two bowls,' and so on.

children.text: samasthūlānāmeva saṃpuṭaṃ bhavati na tu mahadatyalpayoriti ||
children.translated_text: An enclosure is made only of two vessels of equal size, not of one very large and one very small.
Thus the special form of this, distinct from the bowl-apparatus that will be described, has been made clear.
Now he explains it in detail with the words 'a four-mouthed stove'.
'Four-mouthed' is said so that the fire may operate evenly everywhere.
There one should insert the apparatus-vessel.
One should seal it.
One should enclose it with another vessel whose mouth is turned downward.
This apparatus is celebrated in the science under the name vidyādhara.
Its use should be understood as for cooking substances of gentle potency with a mild fire.

children.text: ata eva vakṣyati pañcadaśādhyāye kanakasundararase dattvā vidyādhare yantre puṭedāraṇyakopalairiti ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason he will say in the fifteenth chapter, in the Kanakasundara-rasa, 'having placed it in the vidyādhara apparatus, one should heat it with forest cow-dung cakes.'

children.text: atha somānalayantraṃ samāsata āha ūrdhvaṃ vahniriti ||
children.translated_text: Now he briefly states the soma-fire apparatus with the words 'above is fire'.
'In the middle,' and so on.

children.text: adhaḥpātre jalaṃ tadupari uttānaṃ śarāvādi dattvā tatra laghumūṣāmuttānāṃ dhṛtvā tanmadhye biḍaṃ biḍamadhye sagrāsaṃ pāradaṃ ca dattvā dṛḍhaṃ pidhānena pidhāya tadupari kharparaṃ dattvā tatrāgnir deyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Water is placed in the lower vessel; above it one sets an upright saucer or the like. There one should place a small crucible upright; inside it one should put <s>biḍa</s>, and inside the <s>biḍa</s> mercury together with its morsel. After covering it firmly with a lid, one places a potsherd over it, and fire should be applied there.
By this method one should digest mica-essence and the like.

children.text: etadeva yantraṃ sanābhinālaṃ kṛtvāgnimadho dattvā nābhimadhye pāradaṃ sagrāsaṃ dattvā jārayediti prakārāntareṇa rasasāre 'bhihitam ||
children.translated_text: In another procedure, the same apparatus is described in the <s>Rasasāra</s> as furnished with a navel-tube: fire is placed below, and mercury with its morsel is placed in the middle of the navel and digested.
And its textual reading is as follows:
One should place mercury in the middle of the navel of the soma-fire apparatus.
After giving one eighth part of <s>biḍa</s>, one should fill the navel somewhat with an acidic substance.

children.text: kṣārāmlaṃ tryūṣaṇaṃ mūtraṃ rājikā śigru citrakam
children.translated_text: Alkaline acid, the three pungents, urine, mustard, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>citraka</s>:
the practitioner should fill the tube with these, above the navel.
On top of the apparatus he should place a vessel with holes and with an even bottom.

children.text: chidre ca dorakaṃ baddhvā amlaiḥ kharparapūraṇam ||
children.translated_text: And after tying a cord in the hole, the potsherd should be filled with acids.

children.text: rasopari patedbinduḥ stokaṃ stokaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: A drop should fall upon the mercury, little by little, again and again.
The wise man should place fire beneath the apparatus for three days and nights.

children.text: tridinair jīryate grāsaṃ sūtako nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: In three days the mercury digests the morsel; there is no doubt about this.
Thus.
"With holes and with an even bottom" is a qualifier of the potsherd.

children.text: nālaṃ tu kṣārādipūritaṃ kṛtvā kharparacchidrasaṃmukham evocchritaṃ kāryamiti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sense is that the tube, after being filled with alkali and the like, should be set upright facing the hole of the potsherd.

children.text: etadeva yantraṃ nābhirahitaṃ kṛtvā vaiparītyenāgnijalasthāpanena prāptāgnīṣomākhyaṃ pāradabandhakaraṃ bhavatītyapi tadgranthe evābhihitam
children.translated_text: It is also stated in that very work that this same apparatus, made without the navel, and with fire and water placed in the reverse arrangement, becomes the apparatus called <s>Agnīṣoma</s>, which binds mercury:
"Now fire below, water above, and <s>Raseśvara</s> should be placed in the middle.
By the apparatus called <s>Agnīṣoma</s>, it is bound in seven nights."
Thus.
Now he states the <s>garbhayantra</s> with the phrase "the womb-apparatus".

children.text: yatra sarvaṃ yantraṃ bhūmyudara evāvasthitaṃ vidadhyāt tadgarbhayantraṃ nāma ||
children.translated_text: Where one arranges the whole apparatus as situated precisely within the belly of the earth, that is called the <s>garbhayantra</s>.
He clarifies that very thing with the phrase "four fingers".

children.text: caturaṅguladīrghādilakṣaṇāṃ mūṣāṃ vidhāya tanmukhaṃ vartulaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After making a crucible characterized as four fingers long and so forth, one should make its mouth round.

children.text: samyak pidhānasaṃdhānārthaṃ yathoktabhāgaṃ lohakiṭṭaguggulayor gṛhītvā bhāgatrayaṃ mṛdo gṛhītvaikabhāgātmakaṃ lavaṇaṃ gṛhītvā sarvametajjalena saṃmardya tena mūṣāṃ sāntarbahirvilipya tatra dhātvādikṛtapiṣṭikāṃ saṃbhṛtya samyak pidhāya bhūmimadhyagāṃ gajapuṭaparyāptāṃ gartāṃ karīṣamiśratuṣairardhapūritāṃ kṛtvā tatra mūṣāṃ dhṛtvā tadupari garākaṇṭhadaghnaṃ karīṣatuṣaireva sampūryāvaśiṣṭagartāṃ mṛttikayā sampūryāntarvāyupraveśārthaṃ kiṃcidaṅgulīsamaṃ chidraṃ vidhāyāgniṃ dattvā svedayet ||
children.translated_text: For properly closing and sealing it, one should take the prescribed amount of iron slag and guggulu, take three parts of clay, take salt equal to one part, knead all this with water, smear the crucible inside and outside with it, place in it a paste made from metals and the like, close it properly, make a pit in the middle of the ground sufficient for an elephant-heating, half-filled with cow-dung mixed with husks, place the crucible there, fill over it up to the neck of the pit with cow-dung and husks, fill the remaining pit with clay, make a hole somewhat the size of a finger for the entry of air inside, apply fire, and steam it.

children.text: evaṃ nirvāṇāgnituṣādiyuktyā niṣkāsya punastuṣādipūraṇādisarvamantarāntarā kuryādahorātraparyantaṃ trirātraparyantaṃ veti ||
children.translated_text: When it has cooled, one should take it out by the method involving fire and husks, and again do everything such as filling with husks at intervals, for the duration of one day and night or for three nights.
Here the cow-dung heating should be applied in the ground itself.
This is stated in the <s>Rasarājasundara</s>:
"That heating which is applied by experts in the ground itself, in a fire of powdered cow-dung,
is called <s>govara</s>."
Thus.
He states that the sand apparatus is of two kinds, with the word "surasā".
A well-formed <s>surasā</s>, without knots, hollows, lines, and the like,

children.text: gūḍhavaktrām akarālamukhām adrimṛtkarpaṭādinā trivāraṃ saptavāraṃ vā kṛtenāṅgulasthūlena veṣṭitām ātape saṃśoṣitāṃ kācaghaṭīm udarasya bhāgacatuṣṭayaṃ parikalpya triṣu bhāgeṣu pūrayet ||
children.translated_text: with a concealed mouth and not having an ugly opening, wrapped three times or seven times with mountain clay, cloth, and the like to the thickness of a finger, and dried in the sun: after dividing the belly of this glass bottle into four parts, one should fill three parts.

children.text: tasyā garbhe bhāgatrayaṃ kajjalyādinā bheṣajena pūrayet ||
children.translated_text: Inside its womb one should fill three parts with medicine such as black sulphide of mercury.

children.text: evaṃ sampūritāṃ tāṃ vitastigambhīre bhāṇḍe mṛnmaye viśālakharpare pūritavālukāmadhye sthāpitāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having been filled in this way, it should be placed in the middle of sand filling a broad potsherd in an earthen vessel a span deep.
He also states the measure of the sand to be filled, with the words "one should fill that vessel".

children.text: bhāṇḍodarasyāpi bhāgacatuṣṭayaṃ parikalpya tadbhāṇḍaṃ vālukayā tribhirbhāgairmitayā tribhāgapūraṇaparyāptayā pūrayetsaṃbharet ||
children.translated_text: After dividing the belly of the vessel also into four parts, one should fill, that is, supply, that vessel with sand measured as three parts, sufficient for filling three parts.

children.text: anyābhir avaśiṣṭaikabhāgamitābhir vālukābhiḥ kācakalaśīm abhitaḥ prakṣepeṇāvaguṇṭhayet ||
children.translated_text: With other sand measured as the remaining one part, one should cover the glass bottle all around by pouring it in.
The meaning is that it should be made covered up to the neck.

children.text: bhāṇḍamukhaṃ ca maṇikayā viśālanyubjamṛtpātreṇācchādya saṃdhilepādi kṛtvā cullyāṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: And after covering the mouth of the vessel with a <s>maṇikā</s>, a broad inverted earthen dish, and after making joint-smearing and the like, one should cook it on the stove.
He states the measure of the time for cooking it with the phrase "of the grass".
One should cook it until grass thrown on the back of the <s>maṇikā</s> burns.
"Burning of grass" is an indicative mark.
For in the case of vermilion-mercury and the like, cooking is also necessary until a red color arises.
And that color should be known
by the sight of red-colored vapor rising from the mouth of the flask; this should be understood.
"With an internal coating of mercury".
"Coating" is an indicative expression.

children.text: mṛdbhāṇḍe kharparasamāne viśālamukhe'ntastale nyubjaṃ sthāpanīyaṃ yallaghu tāmrapātraṃ tat pāradādigolakopari nyubjaṃ nidhāya mṛllavaṇādinā bhāṇḍatalatāmrapātramukhasaṃdhiṃ vilipya tayantrabhāṇḍaṃ lavaṇakṣārādyanyatamenāpūrya pidhānena pidhāya praharaparyantaṃ śālisphuṭanaparyantaṃ praharaparyantaṃ vā pacet ||
children.translated_text: In an earthen vessel, like a potsherd and with a broad mouth, a small copper vessel is to be placed upside down on the inner bottom; placing that upside down over a pellet of mercury and the like, smearing the joint between the bottom of the earthen vessel and the mouth of the copper vessel with clay, salt, and the like, filling that apparatus-vessel with any one of salt, alkali, and the like, covering it with a lid, one should cook it for one watch, until the rice bursts, or for one watch.

children.text: evaṃvidhamapi yantraṃ lavaṇayantrākhyametad rasakarmaṇi pākamūrchanādikarmaṇi praśastaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: An apparatus of this kind also, called the salt-apparatus, should be excellent in mercury-work, for operations such as cooking and stupefaction.
Now he states the <s>bhūdharayantra</s> with the word "sand".

children.text: garte rājahastamātragambhīre garte hastamātrāyāmavistāre caturasre vartule vā tādṛśe garte rasānvitāṃ pāradagarbhitāṃ mallamūṣāṃ vālukāgūḍhasarvāṅgāṃ nidhāya gartakaṇṭhaparyantaṃ vālukayā prapūryopari kiṃcitpārśve ca dīptavanyopalaiḥ saṃvṛṇuyādācchādayet ||
children.translated_text: In a pit, namely a pit as deep as a royal cubit, a cubit wide, square or round, in such a pit one should place a <s>malla</s>-crucible containing rasa, that is, filled with mercury, with all its parts hidden in sand; then one should fill it with sand up to the neck of the pit, and cover it above and somewhat at the sides with blazing wild cow-dung cakes.
The meaning is that, after covering it on all sides with wild cow-dung cakes, one should set it on fire.

children.text: atra pāradasya yantraṇamātraṃ vālukāyāṃ bhūmāveva vahnistūparyeva garbhayantre sarvameva bhūgarbhe ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the sand apparatus, only the confinement of mercury is in the ground, while the fire is above; in the <s>garbhayantra</s>, everything is within the womb of the earth.
But in the <s>bhūdharapuṭa</s> there is no connection with sand.
Thus the distinction among the three apparatus-heatings should be understood.
Now he states the <s>puṭayantra</s> with the word "in a saucer".

children.text: bhūmitale karīṣarāśiṃ kṛtvā tatra śarāvasaṃpuṭitaṃ pāradaṃ ca dhṛtvāgnimānavidvaidyo ghāṭikādvayaparyantaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: After making a heap of cow-dung on the surface of the ground, placing there mercury enclosed in a pair of saucers, the physician who knows the measure of fire should cook it for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
This is because the contact with fire is extremely close.

children.text: athavā cullyāṃ karīṣāgniṃ dattvādhiśritakharpare śarāvasaṃpuṭitaṃ rasaṃ dhṛtvā kharparamukhamācchādya yāmaparyantaṃ dviyāmaṃ vā pacet ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, after putting a cow-dung fire in a stove, placing the saucer-enclosed rasa on a potsherd set over it, covering the mouth of the potsherd, he should cook it for one watch or two watches.
This is because the contact with fire is rather more distant.

children.text: evaṃ nyūnādhikaḥ pacanakālo rasayogidravyādyudgamaśālitvāvayavaśaithilyakāṭhinyādyanurodhena svabuddhyaiva tarkya iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the sense is that a shorter or longer cooking time is to be reasoned out by one's own judgment, according to whether the substances combined with the rasa are volatile or not, and according to looseness, hardness, and so forth of their parts.
Now he states the <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> with the phrase "sixteen fingers".
With the phrase "the essence of metals".

children.text: viśiṣṭadhātūnāṃ tāpyagairikavimalādīnām anudgamaśālināṃ mṛdūnāṃ ca sattvasya nipātārtham etadyantraṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should know this apparatus as intended for causing the essence of special metals, such as <s>tāpya</s>, red ochre, <s>vimala</s>, and others, which are nonvolatile and soft, to fall down.

children.text: asyāṃ koṣṭhyāṃ madhya ucitāṃ dhātugarbhitāṃ vṛntākādimūṣāṃ saṃsthāpya kokilair mūṣām uparyuparibhāvena pārśvataśca sampūrya yathocitaṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of this furnace one should set a <s>vṛntāka</s>-type crucible, as appropriate, containing the metal, fill above and around the crucible with charcoal, and blow the fire as suitable.
The meaning is: with a small bellows and the like.
And the metals fit for essence-extraction in the <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> are exemplified in the <s>Rasasāra</s>:

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ sasyakaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntābhre vimalaṃ giriḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, magnetic mica, <s>vimala</s>, mountain mineral,
red ochre, blue vitriol, and especially <s>rājāvarta</s>.
For these <s>uparasas</s>, the extraction of essence is done in a furnace.
Thus.
Now he states the <s>khalacarīyantra</s> with the word "where".

children.text: yantrabhūte lohapātra ābhyantaropakaṇṭhe pārśvayor avasañjanārthaṃ valayadvayaṃ kāryaṃ ||
children.translated_text: In an iron vessel that serves as the apparatus, two rings should be made near the inner rim on the sides, for the purpose of suspending something.

children.text: valayamadhye tu praveśārhakoṣṭhakaṃ lauhaṃ svalpapātramanyadvidhāya mūrchitarasagarbhitaṃ tatsvalpapātraṃ praveśya valayayor avasajjitaṃ kṛtvā sthūlapātre kāñjikaṃ prabhūtaṃ dattvā cullyāṃ mandāgninā praharaparyantaṃ svedayet ||
children.translated_text: Then another small iron vessel, a little bowl able to enter between the rings, should be made; that small vessel containing stupefied rasa should be inserted and made to hang from the two rings. After putting abundant sour gruel in the large vessel, one should steam it on a stove with a gentle fire for one <s>prahara</s>.

children.text: tena pārada utthāya kāñjikadrave praviśya tiṣṭhati ata evāsya yantrasya jalāhāryayantram ityapi nāmāntaraṃ kāñjikajalena svalpapātrād rasasya hriyamāṇatvāditi ||
children.translated_text: By this, the mercury rises, enters the liquid sour gruel, and remains there. Therefore this apparatus also has another name, the <s>jalāhāryayantra</s>, because the rasa is carried away from the small vessel by the watery sour gruel.

children.text: mūrchito rasa utthāya khale'ṅgaṇe carituṃ śaknotyaneneti vyutpattyā khalacarītyapi nāma ||
children.translated_text: By the etymology that the stupefied rasa rises and is able to move in the courtyard of the mortar, it is also named <s>khalacarī</s>.

children.text: atra yatsvalpaṃ pātraṃ tatkāntamayaṃ kṛtvā yantre tatpātramadhye pārado dhṛtaśced atiśayena guṇavānbhavati ||
children.translated_text: Here, if that small vessel is made of magnet and the mercury is placed in that vessel within the apparatus, it becomes exceedingly efficacious.
And it is said in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:

children.text: na sūtena vinā kāntaṃ na kāntena vinā rasaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no magnet without mercury, and no rasa without magnet;
from the conjunction of magnet and mercury, the procedure sustains the body.
Thus.
Now he states the <s>tiryakpātanayantra</s> with the words "one should put the rasa".
"With a bent downward tube" means provided with a downward tube attached to a hole near the bent rim.
The other pot is situated at the side, in a lower place.

children.text: tato ghaṭayorvadane ruddhvā pidhānābhyāṃ pidhāya saṃdhilepādi kṛtvādho ghaṭayor vadanayor adhaḥsthitanalikāyojitacchidrayor api saṃdhilepaṃ kṛtvā jvālayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after closing the mouths of the two pots and covering them with lids, applying joint-sealing and the like, and also sealing the joints at the holes connected with the lower tube below the mouths of the pots, one should kindle the fire.
It should be understood that this apparatus is used for purifying mercury until heat arises in the other pot.
He states the <s>pālikāyantra</s> with the word "cup".
A <s>caṣaka</s> is a vessel like a ladle.

children.text: tattu na tiryagdaṇḍaṃ kiṃtu vinatāgra ucchrito daṇḍo yasya tathoktam ||
children.translated_text: It is not one with a crosswise handle, but is described as having a raised handle with a bent tip.
This apparatus is useful for digesting sulphur along with smoke, and it will also be used in procedures such as <s>parpaṭī</s> described by <s>Bhairavanātha</s>.
Now he defines the brick-apparatus with the phrase "having placed a round one".

children.text: mallaṃ gambhīrodaraṃ kṣudraṃ mṛnmayaṃ pātraṃ tadgartāmadhye saṃsthāpya tatraikām iṣṭikāṃ madhyagartavatīṃ ca nidhāyeṣṭikāghaṭakagartasya paritaḥ samantato'ṅgulocchrāyāṃ pālikām ālavālaṃ vidhāya tadgarte pāradaṃ kṣiptvā tadgartamukhe vastraṃ prasārya tacca dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā tadupari samabhāgaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā nyubjamallena gartamukhaṃ ruddhvā mallapālimadhyabhāgaṃ mṛdā samyagruddhvopari vanyopalaiḥ kapotapuṭaṃ punaḥ punardeyam ||
children.translated_text: After setting a small earthen vessel, a <s>malla</s> with a deep belly, in the middle of that pit, and placing there one brick having a central hollow, one should make a <s>pālikā</s>, an enclosing basin, one finger high all around the hollow formed by the brick and the pot. After putting mercury in that hollow, spreading a cloth over the mouth of the hollow and tying it firmly, placing an equal part of sulphur above that, closing the mouth of the hollow with an inverted <s>malla</s>, sealing the middle part of the <s>malla</s> basin properly with clay, a dove-heating with wild cow-dung cakes should be applied above again and again.

children.text: iṣṭikayā pāradasya yantraṇād etadyantram iṣṭikāyantranāmnā kathitam ||
children.translated_text: Because the mercury is confined by means of a brick, this apparatus is called by the name <s>iṣṭikāyantra</s>, the brick-apparatus.
With that, one should perform the digestion of sulphur without smoke.

children.text: jīrṇe ca gandhake pārado raktavarṇo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And when the sulphur has been digested, the mercury becomes red in color.

children.text: atra drutapārade gandhakajāraṇāyāṃ gartāsye vastrācchādanaṃ vastropari gandhakaṃ ca dadyāditi vidhikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the digestion of sulphur in molten mercury, the procedural order is this: one should give a cloth covering over the mouth of the pit, and sulphur on top of the cloth.

children.text: yatra tu baddhasya rasasya gandhakajāraṇā kartavyā syāttadā tu pāradaṃ vastreṇa baddhvā tasyādhastād upariṣṭācca gandhakaṃ dattvā jārayedityanukto'pi viśeṣo bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But where the sulphur-digestion of bound mercury is to be done, then one should bind the mercury with a cloth, place sulphur both below and above it, and digest it; this special point, though not stated, should be understood.
Now he states the <s>Vidyādhara</s> apparatus for extracting from <s>hiṅgula</s>, with the words "having placed it over a pot".

children.text: antastale nihitaśuṣkahiṅgulāyā viśālamukhāyāḥ sthālikāyā uparyuttānāmeva laghusthālīṃ vinyasya sthāpayitvā saṃdhilepādinā ruddhvordhvasthālyāṃ kiṃcicchītalajalaṃ punaḥ punardadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Over a wide-mouthed pot in whose inner bottom dry <s>hiṅgula</s> has been placed, one should place, that is, set, a small pot exactly upside down; after closing it with joint-smearing and the like, one should repeatedly put a little cold water in the upper pot.
Below, in the stove, one should kindle fire for the duration of three watches.

children.text: etadyantraṃ pāradasya hiṅgulād viyujyordhvapātratala ākṛṣṭikaraṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: This apparatus serves to separate mercury from <s>hiṅgula</s> and draw it up to the bottom of the upper vessel.
The use of this extracted mercury will be stated in the sixteenth chapter, in the procedure for <s>Caṇḍasaṃgrahagadaikakapāṭa</s>, and elsewhere.

children.text: atha ḍamaruyantramāha pāradauṣadhagarbhitayantrasthālyupari nyubjāmeva sthālīṃ nidhāya nirundhayet ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the <s>ḍamaru</s> apparatus: one should place an upside-down pot over the apparatus-pot containing mercury and medicine, and seal it.
One should close the joint with clay, cloth, and the like.
Fire should be applied below the apparatus.
This apparatus, called <s>ḍamaruka</s>, is used in the operation of making mercury-ash that goes to the upper bottom.
Now he states the navel-apparatus with the phrase "in the middle of a bowl".
In the middle of a firm, thick, broad earthen vessel one should make a pit.
There one should place mercury and sulphur.

children.text: tato gartasya samantato'ṅgulocchrāyaṃ kuḍyākāraṃ bandhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, all around the pit, one should make a wall-shaped enclosure one finger high.
After that one should cover that pit with an inverted crucible shaped like a cow's udder.

children.text: atrocyamānayā toyamṛdākhyayā mṛdā saṃdhiṃ ruddhvā saṃśoṣyoparisthitasarvamallabhāgaṃ kaṇṭhaparyantaṃ jalena pūrayet ||
children.translated_text: Having closed the joint with the clay now being described, called water-clay, and dried it, one should fill the whole upper part of the bowl with water up to the neck.

children.text: yantrasyādhastācca cullyāṃ vahniṃ prajvālayedityantimaślokena saṃbandho bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And below the apparatus, in the stove, one should kindle fire; this connection should be understood from the final verse.

children.text: atra jalamṛcchabdabodhārthaṃ jalamṛdaṃ tatprasaṅgācca vahnimṛdaṃ ca madhyasthitagranthenāha lehavaditi ||
children.translated_text: Here, in order to explain the word water-clay, and in that connection also fire-clay, he states the intervening text beginning with "like a paste".

children.text: ghanena babbūlatvakkaṣāyeṇa purāṇaṃ lohakiṭṭacūrṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ kaṇaṃ yathā syāttathā saṃmardya tatra guḍacūrṇaṃ samaṃ dattvā punaḥ saṃmardya kṛteyaṃ mṛjjalamṛditi khyātā ||
children.translated_text: Having triturated old powdered iron slag in a thick decoction of <s>babbūla</s> bark until it becomes very fine particles, then adding an equal amount of powdered jaggery and triturating again, this clay is made; it is known as water-clay.

children.text: atha khaṭikāśvetacūrṇadravyaṃ khaḍū cāsa iti vākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: Now the white powdered substance chalk is explained by the expression <s>khaḍū</s> and so on.
<s>Paṭu</s> means rock salt.

children.text: lohakiṭṭaṃ ca sarvametanmithaḥ samaṃ gṛhītvā mahiṣīdugdhena saṃmardya vihiteyaṃ mṛdvahnimṛdākhyātā ||
children.translated_text: Taking iron slag and all these in equal quantities together, and triturating them with buffalo milk, this clay is prepared; it is called fire-clay.

children.text: iyaṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ vahnipātaṃ sahata ityanvarthākhyā ||
children.translated_text: And this name is meaningful, because it withstands a sharp fall of fire.

children.text: etayā ruddho rasastaruṇyā kṛtasnehena baddhaḥ puruṣaḥ ivānyatra gantuṃ na śaknoti ||
children.translated_text: Mercury sealed with this cannot go elsewhere, just as a man bound by affection produced by a young woman cannot go elsewhere.
Some state another name for this apparatus as the water-apparatus.
He will state its use in the procedure for the stone-piercing mercury.
In the <s>Rasasāra</s> too he cited the use of this apparatus for binding mercury.
Now he states the swallowed-apparatus with the phrase "a crucible".

children.text: sthūlamūṣodare praveśayogyām ādyantamadhyabhāgeṣu tatsamavartulāṃ laghumūṣāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should make a small crucible that can enter into the belly of a large crucible and is equally round at its beginning, end, and middle parts.
This apparatus is known as the swallowed-apparatus.

children.text: anena hi svodare ruddhagatiḥ pārado grastaḥ pīḍito mārakabheṣajena mārito vā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For by this apparatus mercury, its motion obstructed in its own belly, becomes swallowed, pressed, or killed by the killing medicine.

children.text: kajjalīkṛtaṃ bheṣajāntareṇa saṃmarditaṃ vā pāradaṃ sthūlamūṣāntastale saṃbhṛtya tadrodhārthaṃ kiṃcillaghumūṣāṃ nyubjāṃ tadudare praveśya dṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā saṃdhirodhaṃ kṛtvā gajapuṭena pāradaṃ bhasmīkurvanti bhiṣajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Physicians place mercury that has been made into <s>kajjalī</s> or triturated with another medicine on the inner bottom of a large crucible; to block it, they insert a somewhat small inverted crucible into its belly, close the joint firmly, and reduce the mercury to ash with an elephant-heating.
"Piercing" means binding.
Now he states the pot-apparatus with the phrase "in a pot".

children.text: sthālyāṃ mṛnmayapātryāṃ tāmralohādi nikṣipya mallena niruddhamukhaṃ kṛtvā tadbheṣajaṃ sthālikādhaḥsthavahninā pacyate ityetat sthālīyantraṃ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: Having placed copper, iron, or the like in a pot, an earthen vessel, and having made its mouth sealed with a bowl, that medicine is cooked by the fire beneath the small pot; this is the well-known pot-apparatus.
Now he states the fumigation-apparatus with the word "having made".

children.text: atra yathoktamānaṃ lauhaṃ pātraṃ vidhāya tatkaṇṭhādho dvyaṅgule deśe jalādhāraṃ laghupātraviśeṣaṃ nihitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, after making an iron vessel of the prescribed measurement, one should make a water-support, a particular small vessel, placed in the region two fingers below its neck.
The word water-support denotes the vessel that serves as a support for holding a dull or inert substance.

children.text: tatra lohaśalākāstiryaṅnidhāya tatra svarṇapatrāṇi vinyaset sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: There one should place iron rods crosswise, and on them set, that is, place, gold leaves.
Below them one should place the fumigating substance that will be described.
Then one should cover the apparatus-vessel with another inverted vessel.
After making a joint-smearing with clay, one should apply fire below the apparatus.
Sheets killed according to the stated procedure become black.

children.text: tatastāni sarase taptakhalve yathāvidhi mardanena pārado bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Then mercury eats those substances in a warm mortar with liquid, through trituration according to rule.

children.text: bhakṣitāni ca tāni pāradodare śīghraṃ dravanti ||
children.translated_text: And when they have been eaten, they quickly liquefy in the belly of the mercury.
Here he states the fumigation substance.

children.text: pāradena sākaṃ gandhakaharitālamanaḥśilānām anyatamasya samastānāṃ vā kṛtāyāḥ kajjalyā dhūpanaṃ tayā kajjalyā bhasmīkṛtanāgena dhūpanaṃ vā svarṇapatrāṇāṃ dhūpanasaṃskārārthaṃ mukhyaṃ dhūpanadravyam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: For the fumigation of gold leaves, the chief fumigation substance is declared to be fumigation with a <s>kajjalyā</s> made with mercury together with either sulphur, yellow orpiment, realgar, or all of them, or fumigation with that <s>kajjalyā</s> and calcined lead.
It remains to be supplied that the fumigation is for silver.
He states that: silver leaves should be fumigated with the stated <s>kajjalyā</s>, or with dead tin.

children.text: yathāyogyair māraṇayogyair uparasair hiṅgūlarasakamākṣikādibhir api dhūpayet ||
children.translated_text: They should also be fumigated with suitable secondary minerals fit for calcination, such as cinnabar, calamine, pyrites, and the like.
"Preparation of a digestion liquid for leaves" means the preparation of a mercury-containing liquid useful for the digestion of leaves.
The steaming apparatus already mentioned is now described under the name <s>kandukayantra</s>, with the words "in a broad pot".

children.text: anye manīṣiṇo dhīrā vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa prāhuḥ yadveti ||
children.translated_text: Other wise and steadfast thinkers, by the method that is to be stated, say "or else".
That is the <s>kandukayantra</s>.

children.text: evaṃ ca teṣāṃ mate svedanīyantram asmād bhinnam eveti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in their view, the implication is that the steaming apparatus is indeed different from this one.

children.text: puṣpādīnām atimṛdudravyāṇāṃ kalkāder vā svedanārtham asya yantrasyopayogo bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be understood that this apparatus is used for steaming very soft substances such as flowers, or pastes and the like.
Now the stone suitable for the designation "mortar" should be as follows.

children.text: yā nīlā śyāmavarṇā vā snigdhādiguṇaviśiṣṭā ṣoḍaśāṅgulakocchrāyā tathā navāṅgulakavistārā caturviṃśāṅgulair ā samantāddīrghā ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: It should be blue or dark-colored, distinguished by qualities such as smoothness, sixteen fingers high, nine fingers broad, and twenty-four fingers long all around.
The connection with what precedes is: that is suitable for a mortar.
The grinding stone, however, should be twelve fingers long.
Again he states an alternative measure for the mortar-stone, with the words "twenty fingers".
Alternatively, the mortar-stone is twenty fingers long.

children.text: utsedha ucchrāye ca daśāṅgulā kāryeti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The specific point is that in height, that is, elevation, it should be made ten fingers.
But the measure of breadth, "nine fingers", is to be taken just as stated before.
He states the characteristic of excellent clay for a crucible, with the word "clay".
It is whitish, with coarse grains, or with red-mixed whitish grains.
"Potter's clay" is the clay used as material for producing potter's vessels.
Now he states the common clay useful for all crucibles, with the words "that clay".
"With burnt husk".

children.text: caturthāṃśena dagdhatuṣayuktā pratyekaṃ tathā bhāgaiḥ śikhitraiḥ kokilair hayaladdināśvaśakṛtā ca yuktā sā praśastā ||
children.translated_text: That clay is excellent when combined with one fourth part burnt husk, and likewise with separate portions of peacock dung, cuckoo dung, and horse dung.
He states the substances to be mixed into crucible clay by one fourth part, with the words "white stones".
They are also called <s>gāra</s>.
And they are to be taken only when burnt.
Now he states the <s>yogamūṣā</s>, with the words "burnt <s>gāra</s>".

children.text: dagdhā gārā vajraprasavāḥ śvetapāṣāṇā dagdhaṃ śālituṣaṃ ca pratyekaṃ caturthāṃśena taistathā tattadviḍacūrṇaiśca miśritā yā praśastā valmīkamṛttikā tayā vihitā ghaṭitā mūṣā yogamūṣeti kīrtyate ||
children.translated_text: A crucible made, that is, formed, from excellent ant-hill clay mixed with burnt <s>gāra</s>, diamond-producing white stones, and burnt rice husk, each in one fourth part, and likewise with the powders of the respective <s>viḍa</s>s, is called a <s>yogamūṣā</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ cābhrakasattvāder jāraṇāyāṃ viśiṣṭo yo yo viḍastena vilepitā tenaiva kāryā ||
children.translated_text: And for the digestion of mica-essence and the like, it should be smeared with whatever particular <s>viḍa</s> is specific for that operation, and should be made with that very substance.

children.text: atha jāraṇāyāṃ sā pāradagarbhitā koṣṭhīyantre bhastrikayā dhmātā cettayā sādhito jāritatāmrasattvādiḥ khoṭādirūpaśca pārado guṇavattaro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Now, if in digestion that crucible, impregnated with mercury, is blown with bellows in a furnace apparatus, mercury prepared by it, digested with copper-essence and the like and having the form of a lump and so on, becomes more excellent in quality.
Thus the implication is that this <s>yogavāhinī mūṣā</s>, the carrier of the operation, is meaningfully named <s>yogamūṣā</s>.
Now he states the crucible that melts base, not very hard stones, hard stones beginning with diamond, essences, and gems, with the word "<s>gāra</s>".
The <s>gāra</s>s are white, diamond-producing stones.
The earthworm-washed substance mentioned in the chapter on definitions is to be taken.
Flax fibers and burnt husks: these are mutually equal.

children.text: taiḥ samā samabhāgā prāguktalakṣaṇā mūṣopādānamṛd ekatra kṛtvā mahiṣīdugdhena saṃmardya saṃskṛtā ceyaṃ mṛtkrauñcikāpakṣamātraṃ nānāvidhamūṣārūpo yo bhāgo yantratulyastannirmāṇārthaṃ praśastatvena bahuṣu grantheṣu kathitā ||
children.translated_text: Together with them, clay for making a crucible, having the previously stated characteristics and equal to them in equal parts, is put together, kneaded with buffalo milk, and prepared; this clay, equal to the wing of a krauñca bird, is praised in many treatises for making the various crucible-shaped parts that are comparable to an apparatus.
This is because a crucible made from it is difficult for fire to break for a long time in tasks such as extracting essence.
And because, being furnished with earthworm-substance, it is useful for rapid melting.

children.text: tayā saṃskṛtayā mṛdā vihitā mūṣā śāstre vajradrāvaṇaketi khyātā ||
children.translated_text: A crucible made from clay prepared with that is known in the śāstra as a diamond-melting crucible.
Now he states the <s>gāramūṣā</s>, with the word "burnt".

children.text: dagdhā ye mṛttikāpekṣayā ṣaḍguṇā gārāstadviśiṣṭāstathā lohakiṭṭā aṅgārā nirvāṇāgnayaḥ kokilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those burnt <s>gāra</s>s, six times as much as the clay, are specified; likewise iron slag, charcoal, extinguished firebrands, and coke.
Likewise flax fibers, known as <s>tāga</s>.

children.text: te ca pratyekaṃ caturthāṃśamitāstairyuktā yā kṛṣṇavarṇā mṛttatkṛtā mūṣā śāstre gāramūṣeti parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: A black-colored clay joined with these, each measured as one fourth part, and the crucible made from that, is proclaimed in the śāstra as a <s>gāramūṣā</s>.
The implication is that among the effective substances here, those stones possess the greater share.
Now he states the excellent crucible, with the word "diamond".
"Diamond" means a gem-diamond.
If that is unavailable, <s>vaikrānta</s> should be taken.
Charcoals are fireless cokes forcibly extinguished by the scattering of clay dust.
Likewise burnt husks.
And all are mutually equal in part.
Clay four times as much as all of them, and <s>gāra</s>, that is, white stones, equal to that, are used.
A crucible made from this is called a <s>varamūṣā</s>.
Because here a diamond, excellent and of great value, is one of its ingredients.
Now he states the <s>varṇamūṣā</s>, with the word "stone".
"Stones" means red stones.

children.text: samabhāgaiśca taiḥ sahitā yā raktā raktavarṇā mṛttikā tayā sādhitā vihitā mūṣā varṇamūṣeti proktā ||
children.translated_text: A crucible prepared, that is, made, with red, red-colored clay mixed together with these in equal parts is called a <s>varṇamūṣā</s>.

children.text: yasmādiyaṃ niyujyata upayujyate nirvāhaṇena dhātoḥ pāradasya vā raktavarṇotpādanārtham ||
children.translated_text: For this is employed, that is, used, by the extracting operation for producing a red color in metal or mercury.
And it is stated in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>:
"Made smooth by being triturated with stone, heated after being impregnated with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice,
it should be rubbed and heated until it reaches a state of non-rising.
When that has been extracted into silver until it becomes pleasingly yellow,

children.text: hemnā samena militaṃ mātrātulyaṃ bhavet kanakam ||
children.translated_text: mixed with an equal amount of gold, it becomes gold equal to it in measure."
Thus.
Here the extracting operation should be performed in this crucible.
The red group and the white group will be explained later in this very chapter.
Now he states the <s>viḍamūṣā</s>, with the phrase "arisen from the clay of the respective <s>viḍa</s>".

children.text: abhrasattvajāraṇasvarṇajāraṇopayogīni yāni vaḍavānalādiviḍāni yathoddiṣṭarasādibhāvitāni cūrṇāni tathā sarvalohādijāraṇopayogiviḍātmakaścūrṇaḥ paribhāṣādhyāye viḍavarṇanāvasare prāguktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>viḍa</s> powders such as <s>vaḍavānala</s> and others, useful for digesting mica essence and for digesting gold, are impregnated with the prescribed mercury and other substances; likewise a powder consisting of <s>viḍa</s>, useful for digesting all metals and the like, has already been stated earlier in the chapter on definitions, on the occasion of describing <s>viḍa</s>.

children.text: tathā pūrvoktā nānāvidhā pāṇḍurādimṛttadudbhūtā tatsiddhā tathā tattadviḍair grāsajāraṇasādhanair viśiṣṭaiścūrṇairantarvilepitā yā mūṣā sā viḍamūṣetyucyate ||
children.translated_text: A crucible produced from, prepared from, the various previously mentioned pale and other clays, and internally coated with the respective <s>viḍa</s> powders, special powders that serve for digesting the morsel, is called a <s>viḍamūṣā</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ mūṣā dṛḍhakāyakararasāyanavidhau sādhanatvena dehārthā dehopayoginītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This crucible is for the body, meaning useful for the body, as an instrument in the procedure of rasāyana that makes the body firm and strong.
Likewise it is useful for the calcination of metals.
For this very reason it is for metals.

children.text: tathā artho dhanaṃ tathā suvarṇādyutpādanavidhau dhātuvāde sādhanatvenārthārthā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>artha</s> means wealth; so, as an instrument in the procedure for producing gold and the like, in metallurgy, it is for wealth.

children.text: tathā kāsaghnaratnakaraṇḍakarasārśonāśakasarvalokāśrayarasaprabhṛtinānāvidharogaghnarasavidhau sādhanatvena yogārthā cetīyaṃ caturvidhakāryopayoginī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, as an instrument in procedures for various disease-curing mercurial preparations such as those that cure cough, the <s>Ratnakaraṇḍaka</s> rasa, those that destroy piles, and the <s>Sarvalokāśraya</s> rasa, it is for medicinal formulas; thus this is useful for four kinds of purposes.
Now, for the unfailing melting of diamond alone, he states the <s>vajramūṣā</s>, with the word "dung".
With "hair" and "water-cloud".
"Hair" means human hair.
"Root of cloud-sound" means the root of <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ mūṣā dravadraveṇa vyathitā satī antaḥsthataijasadravyayogasaṃyogena bāhyāgnisaṃyogena ca saṃtataṃ pīḍitā satyapyagniṃ sahate ||
children.translated_text: When this crucible is distressed by a flowing liquid, and when it is constantly compressed by contact with the fiery substances inside and by contact with external fire, even then it withstands the fire.
He states the <s>vṛntākamūṣā</s>, with the phrase "eggplant-shaped".
It is twelve fingers in measure.

children.text: dvādaśāṅgulaṃ dīrgham ūrdhvam uttānamūṣāyā ūrdhvatanamukhabhāgo dhattūrapuṣpavat krameṇa vistīrṇastadvadeva ca saṃśleṣeṇa tricatuṣkoṇayuto dhmānāvasare pihite'pi mukhe sati tatkoṇamārgeṇāntaḥsthadhūmasya bahirnirgamanārthaṃ koṇaghaṭanenaiva tanmukhaṃ sacchidraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: It is twelve fingers long. The upper, upward-facing mouth-part of the upright crucible gradually widens like a dhattūra flower, and in the same way, by its joining, is furnished with three or four angles. At the time of blowing, even when the mouth is closed, its mouth remains perforated by the formation of angles, so that the smoke inside can exit outward by the path of those angles.
And that mouth is eight fingers wide; the sense is that it measures eight fingers by the encircling of a circular thread.
Now he states the <s>gostanamūṣā</s>, with the words "of the crucible".
It is "furnished with a crest".
This same crucible, furnished with a peak-shaped lid, is also called the <s>andhamūṣā</s>.
Its use should be understood in procedures such as the combining of paired seeds.

children.text: yatra tu nyubjayā tayācchādanaṃ kriyate tatra pidhānarahitā grāhyā ||
children.translated_text: But where covering is done with it turned downward, one should take it without a lid.
As was stated earlier in the navel apparatus:
"Then one should cover it properly with a crucible shaped like a cow's teat."
Thus.
He states the <s>mallamūṣā</s>, with the word "specified".

children.text: mallaṃ pidhānopayogi vistīrṇaṃ kiṃcid gabhīrodaraṃ mṛnmayaṃ pātraṃ śarāveti loke prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: A <s>malla</s> is a broad earthen vessel useful as a lid, somewhat deep-bellied, commonly known in the world as a shallow dish.
In the twenty-seventh chapter he will state its use in the procedure for the rasa called <s>Madanasamjīvana</s>.
It is also used in many other places.
That very thing is stated with "<s>parpaṭī</s> and so forth".
He states the fired crucible for the <s>parpaṭī</s> and other rasas described in the thirteenth chapter, which require only slight heating, with the word "potter".

children.text: vastramayapoṭalīva bheṣajagarbhitaṃ bheṣajamayamūṣā kapardikāśaṅkhādi bhūmau gajapuṭādinā pācayitum yatra pātrāntare dhriyate pākottaram ācchādanasahitaṃ ca gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: Where a medicine-filled, medicinal crucible, such as a cowrie shell or conch shell, like a cloth bundle, is placed in another vessel in order to be cooked in the ground by an elephant-heating and the like, and after cooking is taken up together with its covering,

children.text: yathā rājayakṣmacikitsāyāṃ mṛgāṅkapoṭalīvidhau sa rasaḥ poṭalītyucyate ||
children.translated_text: as in the treatment of royal consumption, in the procedure for the <s>Mṛgāṅkapoṭalī</s>, that rasa is called a <s>poṭalī</s>.
Now he states the <s>golamūṣā</s>, with the word "mouthless".

children.text: gatvaradravyaṃ pāradarasakamanaḥśilāharitālaprabhṛti madhye dattvā kulālena yā nirmukhaiva vidhīyate etatsamā tāmramūṣā rasahṛdaye 'ṣṭādaśāvabodhe 'bhihitā ||
children.translated_text: A mouthless crucible made by a potter, with volatile substances such as mercury, calamine, realgar, and orpiment placed in the middle, is similar to the copper crucible described in the eighteenth chapter of the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>.
For this very reason that example is not useful here.
An example of the use of an earthen one is not found.
Now he states the <s>mahāmūṣā</s>, with the word "bottom".
With "iron" and "mica".
Here by the word "iron" lodestone should be understood.
It has a yellow streak inside and has been purified by treatment with goat's blood.

children.text: piṇḍībaddhasya koṣṭhayantrodare mūṣāyāṃ laghubhastrayā dhamanādbhavati sattvanipātanam ||
children.translated_text: When it has been bound into a lump and blown with a small bellows in a crucible inside the furnace-apparatus, the deposition of essence takes place.
He states the <s>maṇḍūkamūṣā</s>, with the word "frog".
The depth, length, and circumference of a crucible of that form should be made to measure six fingers.

children.text: upari mṛttikayā tām caturaṅgulamitam ācchādya bhūmipṛṣṭhoparītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After covering it above with clay to a measure of four fingers, that is, above the surface of the ground.
He states the pestle-crucible with the word "crucible".
Mercury bound in a wheel will be described in the twenty-second chapter.

children.text: alpāgnisādhyasya dravyapākasya sādhanāya mūṣā nānāvidhā uktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Various kinds of crucibles have been described for accomplishing the cooking of substances that can be effected by a small fire.

children.text: saṃprati prabhūtāgnisādhyasya dravyapākasya sādhanārthaṃ vividhāḥ koṣṭhīr vaktukāmaḥ prathamaṃ tāsāṃ prayojanamāha sattvānāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Now, wishing to describe various furnaces for the purpose of accomplishing the cooking of substances that requires abundant fire, he first states their purpose with the phrase "of the essences".

children.text: mūṣāmṛdaiva koṣṭhīr vidadhyād ityabhiprāyeṇaivātra koṣṭhīnāṃ mṛdviśeṣo noktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the intention that the furnaces should be made only from crucible-clay, no particular kind of clay for the furnaces is stated here.

children.text: rasaratnākare tu mṛttikādravyāṇāṃ pramāṇamapi spaṣṭaṃ kṛtvābhihitam ||
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>, the measure of the clay-ingredients too has been stated clearly.
And the text of that work is as follows:
Burnt brick-dust, burnt husks, and anthill clay,

children.text: ajāśvānāṃ malaṃ dagdhaṃ yāvat tat kṛṣṇatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and the dung of goats and horses, burnt until it has become black:
leaves of stone-breaker, black clay, each in equal portions,
should be kneaded with the liquids of <s>vajravallī</s>, or ground firmly for a day.
With that one should make furnaces, bent tubes, and diamond-crucibles.
The name <s>koṣṭhī</s> is well known for an earthen enclosure.
And it is of two kinds.
A ground-furnace and a movable furnace.
The furnace-apparatus stated previously is called the movable furnace.
But all those now being described are ground-furnaces.
And they are of two kinds.
By the distinction of an open furnace and a furnace with a cover.
First he states the covered furnace with the phrase "royal cubit".
It is so called because its height, its elevation, is measured by that, namely a cubit with a quarter added, consisting of thirty fingers.
It is so called because its length and breadth are only half of that.

children.text: tathā caturasrā catuṣkoṇā sarvato dārḍhyāya mṛnmayena kuḍyena bhittyā bahirveṣṭitā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, it should be made square, four-cornered, and surrounded outside on all sides by an earthen wall, a partition, for firmness.

children.text: tena catasṛṣu dikṣu catasro bhittayaḥ sambhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus there are four walls in the four directions.

children.text: ekabhittāviti sāmānyata uktamapi yogyatayā pūrvabhittau paścimabhittau veti viśeṣārthe paryavasyati ||
children.translated_text: Although it is stated generally as "in one wall," by suitability it resolves into the specific meaning "in the eastern wall or in the western wall."

children.text: tasyāṃ diśi sthitāyāṃ bhittau dvāraṃ vitastyā saṃmitaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: In the wall situated in that direction, a door should be made measured by a span.

children.text: yadvitastimitaṃ dīrghaṃ sūtraṃ tadvartulaṃ nidhāyāntaravakāśo yāvān sambhavati tanmitaṃ vartulaṃ caturaṅgulamitam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, taking a string measured by a span and placing it in a circle, as much internal space as is possible, a circle measuring four fingers, is meant.
For the purpose of examining the internal flame, which indicates the time for the emergence of the essence, one should make it.
For that purpose, light is necessary.

children.text: sa tu prācyāṃ pratīcyāṃ vādhikyena labhyata iti prakāśayogyatvād viśiṣṭā digevātra gṛhītā ||
children.translated_text: And that is obtained especially in the east or west; therefore, because it is suitable for illumination, a particular direction alone is taken here.

children.text: taddvārasyādhobhāgo dehalī dvāradehasaṃrakṣikā sā dvitryaṅgulamitā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: The lower part of that door is the threshold, which protects the body of the door; it should be made to measure two or three fingers.

children.text: tādṛgdehalyā adhobhāge bhūtalaṃ saṃlagnaṃ pūrvavadeva sārdhavitastimitasūtreṇa paricchinnam arthāt ṣaḍaṅgulaṃ vartulaṃ dvāraṃ bhastrāyojanāya kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Below such a threshold, at ground level, a round door, delimited as before by a string measuring a span and a half, that is, six fingers across, should be made for fitting the bellows.

children.text: atra vitastidīrghā tāvad bhittireva sārdhavitastidīrghā ca dvāradvayārthaṃ paryāptā na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Here a wall only a span long, and even one a span and a half long, is not sufficient for the two doors.
Therefore it is said, "measured by the string, and round."

children.text: kecittu kramanimnabhūminikhātatiryaggartābhāgo'pi sārdhavitastimānārthaṃ saṃgrāhya iti noktasūtradairghyamānāpekṣā lohakārāṇāṃ tathaiva saṃpradāyo'pi saṃprati dhmānavidhau dṛśyata iti vadanti ||
children.translated_text: Some say that the portion of the transverse pit dug in the gradually lower ground should also be included for the measure of a span and a half, since even now the tradition of blacksmiths is seen in just that way in the procedure of blowing, without regard to the measure of the stated length of the string.
But that is not proper.
Because such a pit-section will be described in the subterranean furnace.

children.text: ūrdhvabhāge koṣṭhikāyā uttarāṅgasyordhvāṅgasya ca kartavyā yā bhittiḥ sā caturvidhāpi prādeśapramitā daśāṅgulamitaivārthācchikhākāravat saṃkucitā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: In the upper part of the small furnace, the wall that is to be made for the upper member and upper part should, in all four forms, be measured by a <s>prādeśa</s>, that is, ten fingers; in effect it should be made contracted like a crest.

children.text: śikhāsthāna ūrdhvaṃ dvāraṃ tu prādeśamitāyāmavistāram eva kāryam ||
children.translated_text: At the crest-place above, the door should be made only with a length and breadth measured by a <s>prādeśa</s>.

children.text: tatastaddvāraṃ ceṣṭikayā ruddhvā prāguktavitastimitaṃ dvāraṃ ca kokilaiḥ samāpūrya dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after closing that door with a brick and filling the previously mentioned span-sized door with charcoal, one should blow.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā ruddhvā dhamettadāha prathamaṃ śikhitrān kokilān dhmānārham abhrakādidravaṃ cordhvadvāreṇa krameṇa nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having done what should one close and blow? He explains: first, through the upper door one should put in, in order, fire-charcoals and the mica or other substance fit for blowing.

children.text: kiṃ tad dhmānadravyaṃ piṇḍīkṛtaṃ bhāgaśaḥ sakṛdeva vā nikṣiped ityākāṅkṣāyāmāha sattvapātanagolān iti ||
children.translated_text: If there is the question, "Should that blowing-material be put in as a lump, in parts, or all at once?" he says, "the balls for causing the fall of essence."

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ pratiprakṣepakālāvasaraṃ saṃtataṃ dhmātvā yadāṅgārāḥ kārśyaṃ prāpnuyuḥ śvetabhasmāvṛtāśca bhaveyustadā punaḥ kokilān dattvā punardhamanaṃ kāryam ||
